name: BotDisplayText

variants.name: Raw
variants.doc:
Pass-through. Native renders `value` verbatim — no ICU, no grouping.
For ids, symbols, already-final wire strings, and fixed labels.

variants.name: Placeholder
variants.doc:
Native renders the "--" placeholder. Default for an absent / unloaded
value, so a freshly-constructed state shows "--" rather than blank.

variants.name: Number

fields.name: min_digit
fields.doc: Minimum display precision (trailing-zero pad). `0` = no minimum.

variants.doc:
A number Rust has applied precision + sign to (locale-neutral, no
grouping). Native runs `formatICUNumber(value, locale)` to add the
thousands separator for the device locale. Optionally colored.

`min_digit` is the MINIMUM display precision (decimal places padded with
trailing zeros). `0` means "no minimum" → native renders with
`maxPrecision` (trailing zeros dropped, the common case). A non-zero
value (e.g. the History grid-profit's legacy `minDigit = 2`) makes native
render with `minMaxPrecision(min_digit, MAX)` — Rust has already applied
the MAX/round, so the only render effect is padding to `min_digit`.

variants.name: Percent

fields.name: precision
fields.doc: Fixed display precision (decimal places of the scaled percent).

fields.name: min_digit
fields.doc:
Minimum display precision (trailing-zero pad). `0` = no minimum;
otherwise native uses `minMaxPrecision(min_digit, precision)`.

fields.name: pre_scaled
fields.doc:
`true` ⇒ `value` is already ×100-scaled and rounded (native scales
×1); `false` ⇒ `value` is the raw ratio (native scales ×100).

variants.doc:
A percent value. Native runs `formatICUPercent(value, scale, precision)`,
which applies the locale grouping and the locale-correct `%` placement.
`precision` is the fixed display precision (legacy `fmtPnlPercent` uses 2;
`formatPercent(_, precision = 0)` uses 0). Optionally colored.

`pre_scaled` controls the ×100 step (native maps it to the ICU `scale`):
* `false` (the common case) — `value` is the **raw unscaled** ratio
(e.g. "0.125" for 12.5%); native scales by ×100. Used by every
ratio/rate/APR field, where Rust only applies the business clamp and
passes the raw ratio through (FLOOR/DOWN, byte-identical to legacy
`fmtPnlPercent`).
* `true` — Rust has **already** applied the ×100 AND the per-sign
rounding via `Decimal`, so `value` is the final pre-scaled magnitude
(e.g. "1.20" for 1.20%); native scales by ×1 (no-op) and FLOOR-renders
the already-rounded value. Used by the est-profit-margin / proportion
fields whose legacy leaves round UP or per-sign — which the renderer's
fixed FLOOR cannot reproduce, so the rounding must happen in Rust.

A `bool` (not an `f64` scale) because the money-math fence forbids `f64`
on the public-types surface, and the only two scales in play are ×100 and
×1 — a binary "did Rust pre-scale?" distinction.

`min_digit` mirrors `Number.min_digit`: the MINIMUM display precision
(trailing-zero pad). `0` means "no minimum" → native renders the scaled
value with `minMaxPrecision(0, precision)` (trailing zeros dropped, e.g.
the create-flow `formatPercent(_, minPrecision = 0)` family). A non-zero
`min_digit` makes native render with `minMaxPrecision(min_digit,
precision)`. Every legacy call site sets `min_digit == precision` (its
fixed-precision keep-zeros behaviour is min==max), so the byte output is
unchanged; the new create-flow `percent_min_max_display` leaf is the only
caller that passes `min_digit < precision`.

variants.name: Wrapped

fields.name: min_digit
fields.doc:
Minimum display precision (trailing-zero pad), like [`Self::Number`]'s.

`2`/`2` is the LEGACY-PARITY pair, **not a default**: it reproduces the bare
`formatICUNumber()` this arm used to call on ANDROID, whose own defaults are
`RoundingMode.DOWN` + `Precision.fixedPrecision(2)` (`OKTNumberF.kt:237-243`),
so a producer passing it renders byte-identically to before these fields
existed. There is no defaulted path in either direction: a Rust struct-variant
literal must list every field, and the `#[uniffi(default)]` that would have
defaulted the GENERATED NATIVE constructors is deliberately absent (see below).
Every producer and every native construction site passes both explicitly.

BOTH platforms consume the pair, and resolve it identically: Android's
`BotDisplayTextRenderer.wrappedPrecision` and iOS's
`BotDisplayTextFormatHelper.numberString` both render `minMax(min_digit,
max_digit)` at DOWN rounding — fixed when `min == max`, max-only (trailing
zeros dropped) when `min_digit == 0`. iOS previously rendered every `Wrapped`
wide regardless of payload, so adopting this pair also RETIRES that
divergence: a `2`/`2` field now pads `.00` on iOS as it already did on
Android.

**NOT `#[uniffi(default = 2)]`, deliberately.** The Swift generator renders a
field default INSIDE the enum case declaration (`bindings/swift/templates/
macros.swift` `field_list_decl`, called from `EnumTemplate.swift:15`) — i.e.
`case wrapped(…, minDigit: UInt8 = 2)` — and Swift forbids a default argument in
an enum case declaration, so the whole generated Swift file would fail to compile.
uniffi RECORD fields are safe; enum VARIANT fields are not, and no uniffi fixture
covers this path. Every native construction site therefore passes both explicitly.

fields.name: max_digit
fields.doc:
Maximum display precision. Set this to the precision RUST ALREADY
ROUNDED AT, with `min_digit: 0`, to opt into a wide money render
(sub-cent values survive, trailing zeros stripped).

Native's rounding mode is then provably inert: it caps at exactly the
precision Rust used, so it can never re-round — which is what
`renderConvertor`'s "must never re-round … idempotent caps" contract
requires. That is why no rounding-mode field is needed here.

variants.doc:
A value wrapped with an optional prefix and/or suffix, e.g. "<0.01 BTC"
or "100 – 200 USDT". Native ICU-formats `value`, then concatenates the
prefix/suffix verbatim. Optionally colored.

doc:
One rendered display value for a single bot-detail field.

Rust fills the variant; native renders it. Color is optional per the four
real cases: some numbers carry color (`Some(_)`), some don't (`None` →
default text color); some fields are pure pass-through (`Raw`), some need
native locale formatting (`Number` / `Percent` / `Wrapped`).

Where a field also needs its *raw* underlying value (share card / chart /
tap target), keep that as a sibling `String` field on the interactor state
next to this — don't overload the enum.

**Composition is a FIELD shape, never a variant.** A field needing several
operands (a range, a pair, an N-part label) is typed `Vec<BotDisplayText>`
and native renders each element through the same renderer, joining with its
own locale/theme separator — exactly as `core-trading` does with
`Vec<DisplayString>` (`market_info/settlement_delivery_v2.rs`). Rust still
owns the placeholder/single/range decision by choosing how many elements it
emits (1 = single, 2 = range); it never picks the separator glyph, which is
presentation like the `%` placement and colour hex this file already refuses.
A per-shape variant (the retired `PercentRange`) is redundant with `Percent`,
drops its operands' `sign`/`color`, and breaks every exhaustive `switch` on
both platforms — Swift loudly, Kotlin silently via `else ->`.

**Adding a FIELD to an existing variant is a breaking change too, and it breaks
the platforms ASYMMETRICALLY.** uniffi emits one Swift associated value per
field, and a Swift tuple pattern must match arity exactly — there is no `...` —
so every `case .wrapped(a, b, c, d)` turns into a hard compile error that has to
be padded. Kotlin is unaffected: its renderer reads the variant by property
access behind `is BotDisplayText.Wrapped`. Swift therefore fails loudly at build
time while Kotlin keeps compiling, so a field addition needs an iOS leg in the
SAME MMR or it lands as a red iOS build.

only change what a native consumer reads before `update_instrument`
runs, for a field this file already treats as legacy. Do not
"align" this seed to the other fields' contract — it is a different
contract that does not apply here.

name: recurring_charge_currency_price_digit_warmed
doc:
[`recurring_charge_currency_price_digit`] for callers that CAP INPUT: it waits
for the store, and it says `None` instead of `0` when the charge currency did
not resolve.

Two different jobs in one call, both needed by the buy-price sheet:

1. **Waits.** The sheet is reachable from the running-bots list, where nothing
primes the spot biz, so the synchronous read answered `0` every time.
2. **Distinguishes.** After the wait, `None` means the digit could not be resolved —
blank family, no charge currency, an absent or unparseable `price_dig`, or a
warm-up that did not complete — while `Some(0)` means the instrument really is
integer-priced.
The synchronous export collapses both to `0`, and the caller cannot
recover the difference — which is why a fallback applied on `== 0` would
also fire for integer-priced instruments and let a decimal be typed where
none is allowed.

`None` ALSO covers "the warm-up could not complete": `ensure_trade_data_loaded`
returns `()` and swallows its errors, so offline the store stays cold. Deliberate, but
know what it costs you: the caller's fallback fires offline too, so pick one that is
safe to OVER-allow. iOS picks 2 decimals, which is wrong for a genuinely integer-priced
instrument that it could not resolve — accepted there because over-allowing costs a
backend rejection while under-allowing reproduces this bug. `Some(0)` must keep meaning
"really zero", which is why the two are not merged.

A cancelled call also yields `None`, so it reaches the caller's fallback rather than
being a no-op — louder than in the sibling exports, where cancellation degrades to an
empty list.

hypothetical — it broke the iOS build: uniffi gives a Swift Record a memberwise
init with every field required, so `SignalBotDetailCurrentPositionTabViewController

parameter 'botManagedPositionInfo' in call" (iOS unit-test pipeline 13963782 —

after 1s and shows a success toast, everything else dismisses
immediately (`OKTSSignalBotDetailCurrentPositionTabVC.m:284-291`).
Without it the Rust arm cannot tell the two apart and would flatten a
real UX difference.

`#[uniffi(default = "")]` is REQUIRED: this Record is an FFI *input*
(`signal_bot_position_displays(rows: Vec<StrategyPosition>)` is exported),

name: contract_grid_price_to_base
doc:
Convert a QUOTE-entered price to BASE (wire) units — the legacy
`chargeConvertor.toBaseForOrder:` leaf (÷ rate, then truncate DOWN at 16
decimal places). Linear pairs: identity (rate 1). Inverse (coin-margined)
pairs: user-fiat → USD via the exchange-rate reverse.

This is money math feeding order params — it FAILS CLOSED. Blank in →
blank out (caller drops the key). Unparseable in → blank out. Unresolved
instrument → blank out: whether the conversion is identity (linear) or
fiat→USD (inverse) is unknowable without the instrument, and passing the
quote-entered value through would put a fiat number in a base-currency
order field. Native's shape is the same — `chargeConvertor.toBaseForOrder:`
on a nil convertor nil-messages to nil and the param goes out empty, never
as the unconverted input (MR !6635 review thread on this fn). Never
fabricate a 0.

name: bot_set_mkt_close_all_confirm
doc:
Native `getTradeSettingManager()?.setMtkCloseAllConfirm(value, lifecycle)`.

Exists so the Rust arm stops MUTATING native trade settings: the close-all
dialog's "don't ask again" checkbox wrote straight into OKTradeCore, which is
the one thing the two-arms rule forbids outright.

MUST be the `_async` setter. An earlier draft used the sync one on the reasoning
that legacy is fire-and-forget and never inspects the result — true, but
irrelevant: the suffix marks the SERVER WRITE, not the concurrency shape. The
sync impl is `update_config(...)` only, i.e. in-memory, so the checkbox would
have reverted on the next config fetch or relaunch. Legacy persists on both of
its branches (`OkTradeSettingManager` posts `MODIFY_MKT_CLOSE_CONFIRM_TYPE` and
only syncs its cache inside the success callback).

The token is required because UniFFI's built-in async support cannot be
cancelled; the write's `TradeDataError` is mapped into `OKTSFFIError`, which is
the crate's error type implementing `From<OKCancellationError>` that
`with_cancellation`'s bound needs. Note the fallback checker only matches a
literal `#[uniffi::export]`, so it does not see `cfg_attr`-gated async exports
like this one — the rule still applies.

Also note the two handles are not interchangeable: `trade_setting()` yields the
GETTER impl, the setter lives on `trade_setting_handler()`, mirroring native's
own `getTradeDataSettings()` / `getTradeSettingManager()` split.

fields.name: p_time
fields.doc:

fields.name: latest_profit

`None` (key dropped by the iOS dict bridge → ObjC nil) mirrors
native's absent-key semantics: the profit chart's tail-point advance
and staleness reload are nil-gated (DCD-034, graduates DCD-015).

An OBJECT on the wire (legacy `OKTSProfitChartItemModel *`, NOT a
string) — the DCD-034 `Option<String>` modelling made serde reject
EVERY live WS frame with "invalid type: map, expected a string",
killing all detail live updates (DCD-055; typed-Record precedent:
`RecurringProfitChartItem`). Type corrected in place: the field was
introduced on this branch with zero external consumers.

fields.name: source_info

primary info lands, and carries it forward across WS frames, exactly

fields.name: raw_json
fields.doc:
The server's JSON row, for the iOS `mj_object(withKeyValues:)` bridge
onto `OKTSDCDInfoDataModel` — the same purpose as
`ContractGridBotInfo::raw_json`. Value-preserving (every key and
nested value survives, which is all MJExtension needs); it is a
re-serialization of the parsed row, so whitespace and key order are
not preserved.

Keys this Record does not model still reach native through here, so
an absent wire field stays genuinely absent and native's `?:`
fallbacks (`notionalCcy` / `alternateCurrency` / `settlementCcy` →
USDT, `instId` → entry order) fire exactly as on the control leg. The
typed fields cannot do that job: `unwrap_or_default()` turns a missing
field into `""`, which is a present-but-empty value to native, so
those fallbacks never run and the row renders blank.

`#[serde(skip)]` — this wraps the wire row, it is not part of it.
Both entry points assign it AFTER the typed parse, so it is never
expected from the server (the `order_list.rs:87` trap: modelling it
as a required wire key made every record fall back to `Default`).

name: smart_iceberg_shows_margin_mode_tag
doc:
Whether the Positions tab's header shows the margin-mode marker
(`Cross` / `Isolated`).

Native gates it on
`trade.tradeSetting.isSCCAccount || trade.tradeSetting.isMCCOrPMAccount`
(`OKTSmartIceReleatedInfoCell.m::setShowPositionHeaderViewType:`), and those
three predicates are string compares against the account level
(`OKTradeSetting.m:549-563`): SCC == `"2"`, MCC == `"3"`, PM == `"4"`. So
the union is exactly "account level is not the plain trading account".

**A LIVE read, deliberately un-memoized** — same reasoning as
[`smart_iceberg_is_open_close_mode`]: the account level is user-mutable
(an account upgrade lands while the screen is open) and a snapshot on
either side of the FFI would go stale with no parse to heal it.

✅ Unlike `is_open_close_mode`, the cold-cache default here **matches
native**: `get_account_level()` falls back to `"1"`
(`account_config_getter.rs:301-305`), which fails this gate, and native's
nil `acctLv` fails all three of its predicates too. Both hide the tag.

fields.name: px_display

price (DOWN, drop trailing zeros), resolved at the order's own `inst_id`
price digit. `price_display`. Blank px → `Placeholder` ("--").

fields.name: benefit_ratio_display
fields.doc:
Benefit-ratio text — `getBuySellPercentData(px, lastPrice).second` =
`formatPercentWithSymbol((px-lastPrice)/lastPrice, precision=2, DOWN)` =
`formatICUPercent(DOWN, minMaxPrecision(2,2), EXCEPT_ZERO, ×100)`. Rust
applies the ×100 + DOWN-round (the renderer's fixed FLOOR diverges from DOWN
on negative buy-side amplitudes), so this is emitted `pre_scaled`. Empty px
OR empty ticker → `Raw("")` (legacy returns `""`, NOT the "--" placeholder).

fields.name: avg_px_display
fields.doc: avg fill price VALUE — `getBotPrice(instType, instId, avgPx)`. Same leaf as `order_px_display`.

fields.name: order_amount_display
fields.doc:
order qty VALUE — `getBotAmount(instType, instId, sz, ctVal, ccy = ordType==MARKET ? investUnit
: null)` (`changeUnique` magnitude-precision + DOWN, drop zeros). For market orders the ccy
switches the converter to the quote-side (`quoteDig` + investUnit symbol); else base-side
(`baseDig`). `amount_display` at the resolved digit. Blank sz → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: filled_amount_display
fields.doc:
filled qty VALUE — `getBotAmount(instType, instId, accFillSz, ctVal)` (ccy = null → base-side
`baseDig`). `amount_display`. Blank accFillSz → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: fee_display
fields.doc:
fee VALUE — `getBotFee(instType, instId, fee, feeCcy = getBotFeeUnit(...))` spot path:
UP-round + group + drop zeros at the fee converter precision. The precision branch
(`OkSpotBiz.createFeeConverterWithIndex`): `feeDig` when the resolved fee unit == the trade
(base) symbol (buy side), else `quoteFeeDig` (sell side / quote ccy); empty config →
`DEFAULT_COIN_DIGIT(4)` (the `getPrecision().ifNullOrEmpty(4)` fallback). `fee` is `baseFee`
for buy, `quoteFee` for sell. Empty fee → `Placeholder` (legacy NO_VALUE).

fields.name: rebate_display
fields.doc:
fee rebate VALUE — `getBotRebate(instType, instId, rebate, rebateCcy = rebateUnit)` spot path:
DOWN-round + group + drop zeros at the fee converter precision. Same precision branch as the
fee, keyed on `rebateUnit == tradeSymbol` → `feeDig` else `quoteFeeDig`; NO `ifNullOrEmpty(4)`
fallback (empty config → precision 0). `rebateUnit = instId != strategyInstId ? USDT :
(rebateCcy ?: "")`. Empty rebate → `Placeholder` (legacy NO_VALUE).

fields.name: invest_unit
fields.doc:
The order price / avg fill price label unit — `investUnit = instId != strategyInstId ? "USDT" :
getBotPriceUnitWithFallback(instType, instId, displayId)`. Resolved per item.

fields.name: amount_unit
fields.doc:
The order qty / filled qty label unit (non-market) — `getAmountSymbolWithFallback(instType, instId,
ctVal)`. The order qty market-order arm uses `investUnit` instead (the V2 mapper branches on
`ordType == MARKET`, reading whichever applies).

fields.name: fee_unit
fields.doc:
The fee label unit — `feeUnitWithFallback`: `feeCcy.ifNotBlank ?: ccy.ifNotBlank ?: (spot)
getBotFeeUnit(instType, instId, "", side, tradeQuoteCcy)`. Resolved per item.

(StrategyConvert.kt:1774). SPOT sub-orders never hit the `isHistory && instType==FUTURES`
simple-title branch, so this reduces to `TradeTitleUtils.formatSpotTitle`'s SPOT precedence
(`arg-displayId → bizDisplayId → instId`, then `.replace('-', "/")`, no case fold) — the

at the order's OWN `inst_id` (each sub-order carries its instId). Coin title is a pure label
(no sign/color) → `BotDisplayText::Raw`. `#[serde(skip)]` — off-wire; filled by the history
interactor's `apply_sub_order_displays` enrich pass.

constant fed by an instrument+wire ladder (`tradeQuoteCcy` ->

name: smart_iceberg_pnl_ratio_display
doc:
Row 5 — PnL ratio (`uplRatio`), native
`OKTBotDigitalPrecisionUtil.m:166-169` → `OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.m:214-228,
273-306`. Emitted as a **pre-scaled** [`BotDisplayText::Percent`]: Rust owns
the clamp, the per-sign truncation and the ×100; native adds the locale `%`
and resolves the color.

The chain, in order:
1. blank → `Placeholder`; unparseable → `Raw`.
2. **positive-only clamp** — `0 < n < 0.0001` ⇒ `n = 0.0001`
([`PNL_RATIO_POSITIVE_FLOOR`]). Negatives are NOT clamped.
3. truncate toward zero at `precision + 2` dp: `n < 0` ⇒
[`RoundingMode::Ceiling`], else [`RoundingMode::Floor`].
4. ×100.
5. render [`RoundingMode::Floor`] at 2 decimals, trailing zeros KEPT
(`min_digit == precision == 2`).

Color compares the **step-3** value (post-truncation, pre-×100) to zero.
Native's color function has no nil branch, so every rendered row carries a
color.

⚠️ **The clamp is asymmetric and that is the point.** `+0.00001` is lifted
and renders `0.01%` RISE; `-0.00001` is not, truncates to `0`, and renders
`0.00%` NEUTRAL. Pinned by
[`tests::pnl_ratio_clamp_is_positive_only`].

name: contract_grid_lots_display
doc:
Position-tip "Lot" row (TradFi only): the legacy `lotConvertor.
toTargetFormatted(sz).round` leaf. `None` → native skips the row, mirroring
`futures_makeLotConvertor` returning nil.

The gate is native's `instrument.isTradFi(with: coin)` — coin-info `groups`
contains `"49"` AND `instType == "SWAP"`, with delivery FUTURES
deliberately locked out of Phase-1 scope (`OKTInstrumentDisplayUtil
.swift:736-739`, pinned by `OKTInstrumentTradFiSpec.m:66-90`). It routes
through core-trading's `is_tradfi_swap_instrument`, which is the Rust SSOT
for that same group lookup — do NOT re-derive it from instrument fields.

A `lot_size_std`/`lot_sz` field pair was previously used as a TradFi
stand-in. It was wrong in both directions: `lotSz` is a universal
instrument field, so any instrument carrying `lotSizeStd` leaked a Lot row
onto NON-TradFi bots (shipped symptom: a Lot row on SOLUSD CM Perpetual);
and native's `hasEffectiveLotConfigWithCoin` explicitly tolerates a MISSING
`lotSizeStd` (PRD §5.8 Layer-1 defaults cover it, spec `:240-243`), so
requiring it also HID legitimate rows.

TradFi with an empty `lotSz` is native's Layer-2 fallback: the factory
hands back a ZHANG convertor rather than nil (`OKTBiz.m:1162-1166`, spec
`:244-247`), so the row still renders — with a contracts-formatted value.

Algo order type (server field `algoOrdType`). The legacy `getOrderType()`
is `ordType.ifEmpty { algoOrdType }` (StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:404-406):
some bots send the strategy type ("grid") ONLY under `algoOrdType` with an
empty top-level `ordType`. The Spot Grid Parameter tab's trailing-up/down
section gates on `getOrderType() == "grid"`, so the native composer must
apply the same fallback — reading `ord_type` alone wrongly hid the trailing
rows whenever the wire left `ordType` blank. Additive field; defaults to "".

fields.name: cancel_type
fields.doc:
Why the bot stopped (server field `cancelType`). The detail status label is resolved from
THIS, not from `state`: legacy `StrategyConvert.getGridCancelType` maps it to one of 14
reasons ("Stopped manually", take-profit, stop-loss, liquidation, ADL, delisting, ...) and
falls back to the generic "ended" string. Rendering `state` instead collapses every reason
to a bare "Stopped". Top-level plain-serde field, same as the Spot DCA record
(`dca/spot_dca/detail.rs:142-145`). Additive; defaults to "".

when absent (forward-compatible).

doc:
Full parameter set passed to `submit`.

`#[derive(uniffi::Record)]` is required here because the `#[interactor::actions]`
proc-macro exports every action method via UniFFI, and all action parameters
must implement `uniffi::Lift`. This is a framework constraint, not a
promote-on-demand violation — the record is the interactor's FFI surface.

**Percent-field unit — DELIBERATE asymmetry with the create path, do not "fix":**
`tp_pct` / `sl_pct` / `px_steps` / `px_steps_mult` here carry an ALREADY-DIVIDED
fraction (e.g. `"0.02"` for 2%) — `submit()` forwards them to `ParametersEditsRequest`
verbatim, with NO `div_by_100`. This is the opposite convention from
`place_order::SpotDcaPlaceOrderParams`, whose same-named fields carry the raw UI
percent and get divided internally. The caller (native) already applies
`OKTNumberF.formatHundredQuot` before populating this Record on the edit path — the
same split exists in `contract_dca::edit_params::SpotDcaEditParamsInput` vs
`contract_dca::place_order`, so this is an established cross-bot-family pattern, not
a one-off bug. Harmonizing either side alone breaks the wire for whichever native
caller still relies on the current contract.

name: WithdrawActionState
doc:
Submit / liquidation-price-preview channel only — NOT the profits GET.
`LoadingProfits` is a legacy variant kept for FFI compatibility (removing
it would break exhaustive Kotlin `when` / Swift `switch`) but is no
longer set by `fetch_profits`; that GET is tracked by
`WithdrawProfitState::load_state` (`ActionResultState`) instead.
`Idle` is therefore ambiguous by construction — it means "no
submit/liq-price action in flight," not "profits loaded" — so treat
`load_state`, not this enum, as the authoritative answer to "has the
profits GET completed."

name: bot_recurring_seed_universe
doc:
The set of base currencies recurring buy may seed or offer for a given
quote currency, in the store's own order.

Bridges the eligibility filter both native seeding paths run inline
(`RecurringBuyPlaceOrderViewModel.reloadSearchCoins` and the legacy
`OKTSPORecurringVM`): a spot instrument qualifies when its quote
currency is the one being asked about, that quote currency is on
recurring's whitelist, and the instrument is not waiting to go online
(native `isWaitingOnline = countDownModel != nil`).

Returns raw, case-sensitive base currencies — `XQQQ`, never the `xQQQ`
display form. The order is the store's, which is the product's ranking;
callers must not sort it.

Empty means "nothing eligible", which is a legitimate outcome for a
quote currency with no listed pairs and is handled as a silent
no-seed rather than an error. Gate off / blank quote / cold store
(self-warms) also return empty, so a caller cannot distinguish them —
deliberately, because every one of them means "do not seed from here".

name: create_chrome
doc:
Shared host-chrome projection for `BotPlaceOrderActivity` /
`BotPlaceOrderChromeBinder`; mirrors `SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::
create_chrome` / `ContractDcaPlaceOrderInteractor::create_chrome` (see
`BotCreateChrome`'s own doc comment for the field contract).

Field sourcing:
- `pair_label`: `format_trade_title(inst_id, "SPOT")`. The hardcoded
`"SPOT"` inst type mirrors `SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::
create_chrome` for the same reason it applies there: Spot DCA only
ever trades SPOT instruments (the SAME assumption already baked
into this bot's OTHER formatters — see `resolve_profit_digit`'s "For
SPOT the inst family equals the inst id" and `spot_dca::detail.rs::
dca_resolve_price_digit`), and no resolved inst-type field exists
anywhere on `SpotDcaPlaceOrderState` to source anything else from.
`inst_id` itself is `active_instrument` — the pair every action
already serializes its requests against via `observe_instrument`,
not a second lookup. `CTTradeTitle::default()` while no pair has
been observed yet.
- `ticker`: `state.market_price` — on Android the self-fed
`InstTickerDataSource` value (`InstTickerCallback::on_refreshed`), on
iOS the native `set_market_price` push; both land on
`apply_live_market_price` — plus `state.last_px_tone`
(`apply_market_price_tone`, run there BEFORE the field is overwritten
— the same algorithm Contract DCA's `apply_last_px_tone` / Spot Grid's
`apply_market_price` use). Price digit via `create_order_format::
resolve_price_digit(inst_id)` — the same charge-currency
index-config lookup `spot_dca::detail.rs::dca_resolve_price_digit`
already uses for this bot's other price fields (a local
`Trade::instance()` index read, not network I/O — not a second
instrument lookup). Absent/hidden (`Placeholder` / `Neutral` /
`false`) while no positive price has arrived yet — same gate as
Contract DCA's `create_chrome`.
- `toolbar_more_visible`: `true` — the same provisional literal Spot
Grid / Contract DCA / TWAP's shared-host overflow entry use today;
no real business source has surfaced for Spot DCA either.
- `toolbar_strategy_switch_enabled`: always `false` — Spot DCA has no
strategy-selector catalog (no such field exists on
`SpotDcaPlaceOrderState`), so switching strategies from this screen
is never offered from Rust state today. A real, sourced "no", not a
stand-in for missing data.
- `leverage`: `None` — Spot DCA is a spot bot; legacy only paints the
margin-leverage badge for Smart Iceberg / TWAP on a spot-margin
instrument (`BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`, read-only
oracle), a gate Spot DCA never reaches. See `BotCreateChrome::
leverage`'s own doc comment.

fields.name: pair_label
fields.doc:
Formatted pair label (e.g. `"BTC/USDT"`), NOT the raw `inst_id`.

First proposed as a plain `instrument: String` field carrying
`draft.inst_id` — projectable, but rejected: the only place a pair
label renders on the create screen uses `"${baseCcy}/${quoteCcy}"`, a
different, slash-separated shape, so binding to a raw dash-separated
`inst_id` would have been a silent format mismatch (and worse, legacy
resolves a server-driven display-currency alias via `getDisplayId()`
before the slash swap, which raw `inst_id` can't represent at all).
Readmitted once the correct, already-exported, byte-identical
formatter was found: `core_trading::utils::trade_title_utils::
format_trade_title(inst_id, inst_type)` — an explicit Rust port of
legacy `TradeTitleUtils.getTitleByIdAndType`, already consumed by
TWAP's create/detail flows.

Named `pair_label`, not `pair_title` — this crate already has TWO
other same-shaped fields fed by a sibling formatter, and conflating
any of the three risks reaching for the wrong one:
- **`pair_label`** (this field, create screen) —
`format_trade_title` → `format_spot_title`: `display_id ?: inst_id`,
then `-` → `/`, **no case change**. Matches legacy
`TradeTitleUtils.formatSpotTitle`, the oracle for
`BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`.
- **`edit_params::pair_title`** (`SpotGridEditParamsState`, from
`info.coin_title_display`) — a different field on a different
surface, sourced from `core::utils::format_util::coin_title_display`.
- **`detail.rs::resolve_biz_display_id` +
`core::utils::format_util::coin_title_display`** — Detail / Orders
/ History. Do not conflate with this field.

All three now agree on **no case folding** — `coin_title_display`
previously `.to_uppercase()`d unconditionally, a bug fixed 2026-09-04
(it mirrored legacy's MARGIN/CONVERT branch, which SPOT never
reaches; see `core/utils/format_util.rs::coin_title_display`'s doc
comment). They remain three separate formatters for three surfaces —
not duplication to consolidate — because each is keyed to its own
legacy call path and could still be corrected independently in the
future; don't merge them.

established absence, not a blank value, as the "no badge" contract, so
a spot bot is never forced to carry a spurious empty leverage string.

keeps every existing native decode of this record byte-compatible.

an interactor can project it from state it already computes AND a

a strong enough test: a create screen's toolbar title is a static
per-bot native string resource (not Rust-supplied data, so no source);

user tap that Rust does not track (no source). When a bot needs a
chrome field that doesn't exist yet, that bot's slice adds it with a
real source AND a real, shape-checked consumer. See
`SpotGridPlaceOrderInteractor::create_chrome` for the reference
implementation.

name: signal_bot_order_extras_android
doc:
Android twin of the side/reduce-only half of the open-order card.

Native oracle: `getTradeText(instType, side, posSide)`
(OKTradeCore `StrategyConvert.kt:1211-1242`), whose `Pair<String, Boolean>`
second element feeds `getSideColor` / `getSideBgColor` (`:1663-1677`) and thus
the four `tradeRiseTagContent` / `tradeFallTagContent` / `tradeRiseTagFill` /
`tradeFallTagFill` theme attrs. Rust decides the direction; native keeps the
attr->ARGB mapping, whose resolved values are not provable in this workspace.

Two comparison rules that are NOT uniform, and are silent if swapped:
* `inst_type` — native uses `when (instType)`, i.e. structural equality, so
it is **case-SENSITIVE**. `"swap"` falls to the `else` arm.
* `side` / `pos_side` — native uses `equals(x, true)`, so both are
**case-INSENSITIVE**. Mirrored with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`, which is
ASCII-only where Java folds full Unicode. The gap is unreachable from the
OKX wire format (these fields are ASCII enums) but it is a narrowing, not
an exact equivalence, so do not restate it as one.

The `pos_side` arm order also matters: long, then short, then a catch-all that
covers blank and any other value (reachable on one-way-mode rows).

There is no failure path: this is a pure function of three wire strings with
no instrument load, so it cannot raise `instrument_not_found` and returns a
plain `Vec` rather than an `Option`.

name: load
doc:
Load the retained page (page 1 before any load).

Reproduces the **ANDROID** contract bug-for-bug:
`HistoryPositionFragment.onVisible()` re-fires
`requestHistoryPositions()` with the presenter's RETAINED page —
`HistoryPositionPresenter` only resets `page` in `reloadPositions()`
(the empty-view retry) — and its observer appends whenever
`isRefresh()` (`page == 1`) is false, so re-appearing after paging past
page 1 re-appends that page.

iOS is NOT that shape and does not call this. `OKBPagedListVC`'s
`viewWillAppear:` either refreshes page 1 (`data.count == 0` +
`autoRefreshOnEmpty`) or leaves the list alone apart from an
expiry-driven `beginRefreshing`, which is also page 1 — it never
re-requests the retained page. The Swift tab accordingly uses only
`refresh` / `load_more`. Kept unchanged because Android is the caller;
an earlier revision of this doc called the Android fragment "Native",
which is the same wrong-baseline wording that produced the unbounded
`has_more` and the load-more page skip.

`PlaceOrderCondition` (`OKTradeCore biz/trade.kt:1477-1480`,
`spreadRatio`/`unitAmt`). Currently populated only by the Smart
Arbitrage stop flow (legacy's `MODIFY_SPREAD_RATIO_TOTAL_AMOUNT`
close-condition sub-dialog); Grid/DCA stop never sets this.

name: adjust_order_stop
doc:
Adjust grid order stop loss / take profit.

Returns the typed `AdjustOrderStop` Record directly. Empty server
response is folded to `OKTSFFIError::EmptyData` by the use_case.

Six adjust-knobs + `inst_id`/`algo_id` + `cancel_token` push this
past the 6-arg clippy guidance in
`internal_services.md` § "Trait method input shape". Per the
existing pattern in `services/dcd/place_order_service.rs` and
`services/signal_bot/place_order_service.rs`, the FFI surface
keeps the individual params (native binders prefer named args
over a bundle) and the internal trait already takes
`AdjustOrderStopInput`.

`tpsl_trigger_param` is the additive `tpslTriggerParam` advanced block.
Spot-grid TP/SL edit supplies it (`SpotGridEditP.confirm()` always sets
it); contract-grid callers pass `None` and the wire payload stays
byte-identical to the pre-existing shape.

name: bot_contract_lot_size_validation
doc:
Bridge native's contract lot-size validation
(`ContractTradeInputUtils.getAmtTickSizeMsg`, `TradeInputUtils.kt:529-565`).
`amount` is the value in the user's ALREADY-RESOLVED display unit — the same
value `ContractDcaClosePositionBottomSheet` feeds into `TradeInputUtils
.getAmtTickSizeMsg` today — matching what native validates.

Branch selection mirrors native exactly:
* `TradeUnit::U` (any contract type) -> no check, native's own no-op.
* linear (`!is_inverse`) + Coin/Contract -> `lot_sz` converted into the
display unit via the SAME `OriginQuantityToUserSettingUnitConvertor` that
already backs [`resolve_size_unit`] / [`convert_size_to_user_unit`] (no
price needed — native itself passes a dummy `price = "1"` for this
branch, confirming it is price-independent for linear contracts).
* inverse (`is_inverse`) + Contract -> raw `lot_sz`, no conversion (matches
native using `bizInstrument.getLotSize()` directly for this branch).
* inverse + Coin -> no check, native's own no-op.
* `TradeUnit::Lot` -> `None` (cannot determine): native additionally gates
Lot on a TradFi "Rust CEX" flag (`isTradeUseRustV1()`) that swaps the
board-lot step for a `10^-lotDig` TradFi convention this crate has no read
for. Guessing which rule applies risks a wrong lot size, so this returns
`None` rather than silently picking one.
* `TradeUnit::Unknown` -> `None`: native's real trade-unit setting never
produces this value — it is this crate's own fail-closed default
(`map_trade_unit`) when the convertor cannot classify a unit.

`None` also for: gate off / blank instId or amount / unparseable amount /
unresolvable instrument / unresolvable unit conversion. Native's own
"safe-parse-to-zero" behavior for a malformed amount is deliberately NOT
reproduced (`docs/conventions/money_math.md` bans silent-zero parsing) —
callers get "cannot determine", not a fabricated pass or fail.

NOTE the icon URL did NOT come with it: `OKTrade.okts_imageURLForCoin:`
opens with a LOCALIZED special case (if the symbol equals
`pr_trade_general_usds` it returns the localized
`pr_trade_general_usds_image_url`) and then uppercases for an xStock
registry-key stopgap. Rust does not ship localized copy, so that read
stays native — see the tracker's W3-R1 entry.

fields.name: coin_price_display
fields.doc: Placeholder when this leg IS the invest ccy — no price against itself.

fields.name: target_ratio_display
fields.doc:
Target allocation percent, rounded DOWN at 2 (`toLocalizedStringDown(toMax:
2)`) with trailing zeros **TRIMMED** — `min_digit` must stay 0.

fields.name: original_num_display
fields.doc:
Holdings at creation, DOWN at the holdings digit — see
[`Self::cur_num_display`] for which digit that is.

fields.name: cur_num_display
fields.doc:
Current holdings, DOWN at the holdings digit.

The digit follows native `getCoinPrecision`, which branches on whether this
leg IS the invest ccy: the quote leg uses
`getCoinConfigPrecision(investCcy)` (the coin's own `sizeDig`), every other
leg uses the instrument's `baseDig`. `"USDT-USDT"` is not an instrument, so
keying the instrument lookup for a quote leg misses and silently falls back
to 2 — visible on a `balType == "combined"` portfolio holding the quote ccy
as a real constituent.

fields.name: market_value_display
fields.doc: `cur_num * px`, DOWN at the invest-ccy coin precision.

fields.name: current_ratio_display
fields.doc:
`marketValue / mktCap` as a percent — UP for a USDT leg, DOWN otherwise,
both `toMax: 2` so trailing zeros are **TRIMMED** (`min_digit` stays 0).

ONE twin serves two rows: Overview's `getCurrentAllocation` and
Parameters' `getCurrentRatioText` compute this identically. A test asserts
that equality so a change to one call site cannot silently drift.

fields.name: current_ratio
fields.doc:
The SAME quantity as [`Self::current_ratio_display`], but RAW: the
unscaled `marketValue / marketCap` fraction (e.g. "0.35" for 35%), with no
percent formatting and no display rounding — only the wire-format bound
`SP_RATIO_RAW_DP` imposes (20 dp, half-up, because the donut parses this
with `NSDecimalNumber` and its silent failure mode is zero).

Both exist because the two consumers need different things from one
computation: the Overview / Parameters ROWS need the rendered percent
(per-coin rounding: USDT up, everything else down), while the allocation
DONUT needs a number for slice geometry. Reading a rendered percent back
into a number would re-parse a value that was deliberately rounded for
display, and computing the fraction again in Swift would put money math
back on the native side.

EMPTY means "omit this slice", not zero: it carries the donut's two numeric
inclusion rules, so the leg is dropped unless `cur_num * px` AND the
resulting fraction are both strictly positive — which is how native's
per-leg `marketValue > 0` guard and its whole-list `mktCap > 0` guard are
expressed on a per-leg field. Also empty when either operand is absent or
unparseable — never a bogus "0".

fields.name: trigger_cond
fields.doc:
Raw trigger-condition wire literal: `"cross_up"`, `"cross_down"`,
`"above"`, `"below"`, `"cross"`, or `""` when absent.

Populated for `Rsi` (drives `formatTriggerCond` in the RSI alert) and
for `Price` (drives the `formatTriggerStrategy` price branch — cross_up
→ "Price crosses above", cross_down → "Price crosses below", anything
else → "Price trigger"). Swift maps the literal to localized copy;
an unrecognised literal renders `--` there, matching native
`formatTriggerCondWithType:`'s `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` fall-through.

fields.name: trigger_px
fields.doc:
Raw trigger price (`Price` only), `""` when absent.

Native renders it through the instrument's charge convertor at both
call sites, so no precision or formatting decision is made here.

fields.name: thold
fields.doc:
RSI threshold (`Rsi` only), already resolved by native's
`getTholdValue` rule: prefer `oversoldThold`, fall back to `thold`
(`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel.m:213-218`).

The two keys exist because the server is deprecating `oversoldThold`
in favour of `thold` while the order API still writes the old key
(`.h:87`) — picking the wrong one shows a stale threshold, so the
choice is made once in Rust. `""` when neither key is present.

fields.name: time_period
fields.doc:
RSI indicator period (`Rsi` only). Defaults to `"14"` when the server
omits the key, mirroring native's `startModel.timePeriod ?: @"14"`
(`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:178`). An explicitly-empty server value is
preserved as `""` — native's `?:` fires on nil only.

fields.name: timeframe
fields.doc:
Raw K-line timeframe wire literal (`Rsi` only): `"3m"`, `"1H"`, `"1D"`,
… Swift renders it via the localized
`OKTRSITriggerItem.getKLineTimeFrameTitleWithValue:` template.
`""` when absent.

fields.name: delay_seconds
fields.doc:
Delayed-start seconds (`Rsi` alert only), `""` when absent. Swift
formats the number and pairs it with the "Delayed Start" label — see
the `isStartTriggerAction` row of the table above for why the label is
never "Delayed Stop" on this screen.

doc:
Smart Iceberg start-trigger condition — the durable subset of native
`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel` that the Smart Iceberg detail screen reads.

Reached natively as `OKTStgyInfoModel.startTriggerModel`. The native type
carries ~30 members serving grid / DCA / signal bots; only the three
Smart Iceberg consumers below are modelled here:

1. Start Condition **row value** — `OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:163-173`.
2. **RSI detail alert** — `OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:177-188`.
3. **Price detail alert** — `OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:190-198`.

# Rust owns the values and the decisions; Swift owns every string

Every native helper these three call was classified before porting:

| Native helper | Verdict | Where it lives now |
|---|---|---|
| `isIndicatorInstance` / `isIndicatorPrice` / `isIndicatorRSI` | **Business logic** — a two-field precedence ladder, not formatting | Rust: resolved into [`indicator`](Self::indicator) |
| `getTholdValue` | **Business logic** — picks `oversoldThold` over `thold`; the server is mid-migration between the two keys | Rust: resolved into [`thold`](Self::thold) |
| `timePeriod ?: @"14"` (`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:178`) | **Business default** — RSI's default indicator period, not a display string | Rust: resolved into [`time_period`](Self::time_period) |
| `isStartTriggerAction` (`.m:185`) | **Constant-true here** — this Record is only ever built from the entry whose `triggerAction` IS `"start"`, so native's ternary can never take the "Delayed Stop" branch | Dropped; Swift renders "Delayed Start" unconditionally |
| `formatTriggerCond` | **Pure formatting** — a 5-way `OKLocalString` lookup over the `triggerCond` literal (`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel.m:309-331`) | Swift, from [`trigger_cond`](Self::trigger_cond) |
| `formatTriggerStrategy` | **Pure formatting at this call site** — `actionQuestionBtnPrice` only runs when `isIndicatorPrice`, so the method's price branch (`.m:376-383`) is the only reachable one: cross_up / cross_down / else, each an `OKLocalString` | Swift, from [`indicator`](Self::indicator) + [`trigger_cond`](Self::trigger_cond) |
| `OKTRSITriggerItem.getKLineTimeFrameTitleWithValue:` | **Pure formatting** — splits `"3m"`/`"1H"`/`"1D"` into a localized template | Swift, from [`timeframe`](Self::timeframe) |
| `chargeConvertor toQuoteFormated:` (price row + price alert) | **Pure formatting** — instrument-precision + locale grouping | Swift, from [`trigger_px`](Self::trigger_px) |

Numeric scalars stay `String` (precision-preserving) exactly as the native
side already exposes them: it parses each into `NSDecimalNumber` and hands
`toPlainString` — a non-localized, non-grouped rendering — to the display
layer, so passing the wire text through is equivalent. No arithmetic is
performed on any of these values in Rust.

name: SpotDcaDetailEvent
doc:
One-off UI events emitted by the interactor.

All terminal arms surface through durable state fields (`tab_state:
GridTabState`, `is_loading: bool`, `error: Option<String>`, plus the
derived flags `can_pause` / `can_resume` etc. driven by `bot_info`).
The screen does not currently emit transient toasts — Rust no
longer ships English UX copy; native composes localized text from
the durable state fields per `naming.md:139`. Per `interactor.md`
§ "Terminal results surface via durable state, not events", we use the `_PlaceholderEvent`
escape hatch rather than declaring a `ShowToast` variant we never
emit.

name: ArbLegLeverOutcome

variants.name: NoRow
variants.doc:
No matching row — native's `marginInfoByPosSide:` returned nil, or the side
was neither buy nor sell. Native's value is `nil`.

variants.name: NotApplicable
variants.doc:
A row exists but reports its OWN margin mode and that mode disagrees with the
leg's, so the leverage does not apply. Native substitutes
`kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` (`hotFixLever:`, `OKTASPOButtonLineVC.m:454-462`).

variants.name: Value
variants.doc: The leverage to display, verbatim.

doc:
What the lever control should show for one position side.

Three outcomes, kept distinct instead of collapsing into `Option<String>`,
because native has three and two of them are NOT the same thing:
"no row at all" and "a row whose leverage does not apply" render the same
placeholder today but arise from different states, and an empty-string sentinel
is exactly the collapse that produced this screen's earlier defects.

Rust does not emit the placeholder TEXT — `naming.md` forbids user-facing
localized strings here, and `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` / `kOKTPONoLoginLeverValue`
are host constants. The host maps [`Self::NoRow`] / [`Self::NotApplicable`] onto
whichever of its own placeholders native uses at that call site.

name: smart_iceberg_margin_ratio_display
doc:
Row 7 — margin ratio (`mgnRatio`): `treatAsPercentage` (×100) then
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2` — [`RoundingMode::Floor`], fixed 2
decimals, locale `%`.

Emitted as a [`BotDisplayText::Percent`], the SAME variant as row 5. The two
rows end in an identical native pair (`treatAsPercentage` +
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2`), so they must render identically; only the
pre-processing differs (row 5 adds the clamp + per-sign truncation).

Canonical precedent for this exact native leaf:
`public::interactors::grid::contract_grid::detail::percent_down_fixed2_display`
— "renderer-side ×100 + DOWN + fixed 2 + `%`". That helper is private to the
contract-grid detail module and passes the raw value with
`pre_scaled: false`; here Rust applies the ×100 itself (`pre_scaled: true`)
to stay consistent with [`smart_iceberg_pnl_ratio_display`] next door, which
MUST scale in Rust because its truncation happens at the pre-×100 magnitude.

Native sets no `suffixText` on this row, so the cell's key label carries no
parenthesised unit — the `%` rides on the value, as it does natively.

Needs no instrument — pure arithmetic, so it can never go stale.

name: create
doc:
Create the pending-orders interactor.

`last_price` SEEDS the benefit-ratio (`% to fill`) baseline so the first
HTTP render already carries a real ticker, byte-identical to legacy
`GridPendingOrderPresenter` which primes `mapper.lastPrice` from
`requestBatchMarketTicker()` (the bot's market last price) BEFORE the
`tickers` WS subscription delivers a frame. Without it, the per-row
`benefit_ratio_display` was starved (`ticker_price == None`) until the
first WS push, so EVERY row's `% to fill` rendered the empty "" → "--".
The bot's `lastPrice` is the same value the native caller already holds
from the SpotGrid bot-info HTTP fetch (`SpotGridBotInfo.lastPrice`). A
blank seed is a no-op (the WS still fills it live). The `tickers` WS
continues to OVERRIDE this seed on every push, so the live ratio tracks
the freshest price exactly like the legacy `updateBenefitRatio`.

`paramsFromSelf` reflection emits whether or not anyone assigned it, because
a primitive has no "unset" state. Hence its position: last, outside the
assignment-ordered block above.

⚠️ **A JSON boolean, not a string** — deliberately against this struct's own
convention. `reduceOnly` / `major` / `associate` are strings *only* because
`genParams` explicitly stringifies them (`OKTSCommitArbitrageParams.m:23-24`,

applied to it.

construction site rather than threaded through state: the arbitrage
place-order flow never writes the property (zero assignments under
`placeOrder/arbitrage/`; only TWAP and Smart Iceberg set it, off a borrow
checkbox this page has no counterpart to). Kept as a field anyway so a
future borrow rollout has the seam — but do not wire it to anything without
a native assignment to mirror.

name: signal_bot_max_drawdown_display_android
doc:
Android's MAX-DRAWDOWN formatter. Narrowed from an "indicator" catch-all:
the win-rate row does NOT need this — iOS's
`[[num treatAsPercentage] toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2]`
(`OKTSSignalBotDetailViewModel.m:139`) and Android's
`formatICUPercent(DOWN, minMaxPrecision(2, 2), AUTO, x100)` are equivalent, and
a win rate is non-negative so the renderer's FLOOR equals DOWN. Win rate
therefore shares [`signal_bot_win_rate_display`] with iOS.

Max drawdown genuinely differs and cannot share
[`signal_bot_max_drawdown_display`]:

* iOS clamps a positive ratio below `0.001` UP to `0.001`
(`OKTStgyMaxDrawdownUtil.percentFixedNumberFromPlainString`) — "any drawdown
shows at least 0.10%". Android has no such rule; it reuses its win-rate
formatter (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1204`). **Whether Android is simply
missing this product rule is an open question for product/iOS.**
* A drawdown can be NEGATIVE (iOS branches on `isLessThanZero`), and there the
renderer's fixed FLOOR diverges from Android's DOWN — hence the pre-scaling
below.

Android's contract, from `formatIndicatorPercent`
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1204`):
`OKTNumberF.formatPercent(x, roundMode = DOWN)` resolves to
`formatICUPercent(DOWN, minMaxPrecision(2, 2), AUTO, scale = 100)`.

**Pre-scaled on purpose.** `BotDisplayTextRenderer` hard-codes
`RoundingMode.FLOOR` for `Percent`, which equals Java's `DOWN` only for
non-negative input — a negative drawdown would diverge on the last decimal
(`-12.345` -> `-12.34` toward zero, `-12.35` toward -inf). Rust therefore
applies the ×100 and the toward-zero rounding itself, leaving the renderer's
FLOOR a no-op.

Blank -> `Placeholder`: native returns null for a blank ratio and the row
renders `--`. Unparseable -> **ZERO**, deliberately NOT the `Raw`
pass-through its two siblings use, because native's `toBigSafeDecimal`
coerces garbage to zero and the row shows `0.00%`.

Do **not** use [`signal_bot_max_drawdown_display`] on Android. That one
models iOS's three-step chain — a 0.001 small-positive clamp plus a per-sign
4-decimal pre-round — neither of which Android performs. Android has exactly
one indicator formatter, so both rows share this function.

name: replace_with_ws_data
doc:
Replace with an authoritative open-order snapshot. Used by BOTH platforms.

Android `TradeStrategyOrderBillDetailsTask` first applies incremental
socket rows to its private list and then publishes that FULL list. A
second merge would retain rows Android already removed. Empty is
meaningful and clears the tab.

iOS needs exactly the same entry, which is why this is no longer gated to
`cfg(any(test, target_os = "android"))`: native's `processWSData:` has a
snapshot branch as well — `data.count == 0` clears the list and
`data.count > 1` is the "first / timed / full push" that calls
`updateItems:data` outright (`OKTSSignalBotSubOrderDataSource.m:73-82`).
Neither is expressible through the merge entry, which can only
replace-matching / append-new and therefore keeps rows the snapshot
dropped.

This does NOT make `update_with_ws_data` redundant: iOS still routes the
single-row event pushes through it (insert / remove / coalesced update),
exactly as native does.

(szLimit → lmtOrderNumber → sz). The caller applies the presentation
mode:
- tap (`checkAllInput`, `.m:251-259`): render ONLY the first entry
and focus its field — native stops at the first failing rule and
never touches later fields;
- edit (`amountChangeBlock` → `action*EditingEndV2`, `.m:341-390`):

predicates, deterministic where native's read of persisted UI error

Field sourcing:

not re-fetched) and `state.ticker_raw` — the same
`format_trade_title` / `ticker_number` / `ticker_tone` this

non-blank leverage — see `BotTradeHeader.refreshCoinPairsNormal`

INST_TYPE_MARGIN` match as `apply_core_context`), while
`context.is_spot_support_margin` keeps a non-margin-capable pair
from inheriting an account-level leverage. The resolved value
reuses `effective_leverage`, this interactor's own leverage
resolution (no second instrument/account lookup). `None` (not an
empty string) for every other route.

Spot Grid / Contract DCA's shared-host overflow entry use today;
TWAP's own Kotlin fragment (`TwapRustPlaceOrderFragment.bindChrome`
/ `.observe`) also hardcodes `moreVisible = true` at both of its

not a stand-in for missing data.

strategy-selector catalog (no such field exists on

Confirmed against the shipped iOS consumer, not just inferred:
`OKTSDKVInfoDataHandler.m:161-162` renders the row as
`[NSDate fromTimestamp:orderData.nextInvestTime.doubleValue / 1000]`,
and `fromTimestamp:` takes SECONDS — so the value it divides must be ms.
That path is in production and renders correct times, which settles the
unit as firmly as a wire capture would.

An earlier revision of this doc claimed the field was ms "even though"
[`Self::c_timestamp`] / [`Self::u_timestamp`] were seconds. That premise
was wrong — those two are ms as well (see their note). The endpoint is
uniformly ms; nothing here is asymmetric.

`SAMPLE_INFO` carried a 10-digit (seconds) value until this was checked,
so the crate held both spellings for one field while `cTime`/`uTime` in
the very same fixture were 13-digit ms. Both fixtures are ms now.
Nothing in the Rust twin depended on it — `resolve_next_purchase_visible`
(`displays.rs:410-416`) only probes parseability — which is why the
disagreement survived a green suite.

fields.name: fee_list

Wire `feeList`. **Gap R-F5** — see [`RecurringFeeEntry`]. Only the first
entry's `feeCcy` is read (native's `okts_spot_feeCcy()` conformance), but
the list shape is preserved so a future consumer needing the rest doesn't
require a wire-contract change.

fields.name: copy_type
fields.doc:
Copy-trading relationship kind — wire key **`copyType`**.

**Finding R-B19.** Not read for display on this page, which is why the
field audit missed it: its only consumer is the analytics property
`createbot_type` at `BotDetailsOverviewCellBaseViewController:138`, which
calls `OKTStgyInfoModel.createbotTypeForStatistic()` →
`isCopyTradingOrder()` / `isShareProfitFollowOrder()`, both of which test
`followOrderType` — the property mj maps from `copyType`
(`OKTStgyInfoModel.m:49`).

Without it the bridge could never produce `"lead"` or `"follow"`: every
lead-trading and profit-share-follow recurring bot was reported as
`"copy"` or `"manual"` in the Rust arm. Same defect class as R-B15 — a
consumer reading a field the bridge never wrote — but reached through a
derived ObjC method rather than a property, so grepping property names
alone did not surface it.

This is the **top-level** `copyType`, distinct from the one on the
source-model node (which the DCD wave bridged as DCD-013).

`/priapi/v5/algo/marketplace/source-strategy-info` endpoint.

`#[serde(skip)]` because this field is NOT on the bot's info wire
shape — `RecurringInfoStreamUseCase` populates it after detecting
a non-empty `source_algo_id`. Native reads it directly to render
the Parameters tab "From" row.

Latest profit-chart data point. Bridged to iOS as a typed nested
Record so the chart VC can read `profit` / `pnl` / `time` fields
without a JSON parse.

fields.doc:
Wraps the wire `bot.recurring.*` nesting. Use
`bot.as_ref()?.recurring.as_ref()?.<field>` to access. None when the
server omits the nesting.

fields.name: is_start_or_stop_order
fields.doc:
`true` when the bot is mid-transition — native
`isStartingOrStoppingOrderStatus` (`OKTTypes.m:617-620`):
`state ∈ {"stopping", "starting"}`.

Consumed by the Overview info cell's `isStartOrStopOrder`
(`RecurringBuyDetailsOverviewCellInfoViewState.getIsStartOrStopOrder`).

⚠️ Native's helper compares against `OKTOrderStatusTypeGridStopping` /
`…GridStarting`, whose raw values are the **unprefixed** `"stopping"` /
`"starting"` (:565, :567) — NOT `"gridStopping"` / `"gridStarting"`. The
symbol names are misleading; the strings are what matter.

fields.name: is_stopped_order
fields.doc:
`true` when the bot is finished — native's recurring-detail
`isStoppedOrderStatus`: `state ∈ {"canceled", "stopped"}`
(`RecurringBuyDetailsViewModel.isStoppedOrderStatus` +
`…ParametersTabInfoViewState.getIsStoppedOrder`, comparing
`OKTOrderStatusTypeCanceled` (:550) / `…GridStoped` (:577)).

Deliberately does NOT include `"effective"`. `isHistoryOrderStatus`
(`OKTTypes.m:622-628`) does treat `effective` as history, but the
recurring detail page's own predicate does not — and native behaviour is
the spec including its inconsistencies. See the tracker's Native ledger.

fields.name: is_follow
fields.doc:
`true` when this bot was copied from another trader — native
`!infoModel.sourceAlgoId.isEmpty` on the live-info path
(`getTagStyles(isFollowOrder:)` / `isFollowOrder`).

**Gap R-F4 (Wave R1).** Note the two native paths differ: the
running-bot-record path calls `orderModel.isFollow()` while the info
path tests `sourceAlgoId`. This flag mirrors the **info** path, which is
the one the detail page renders from once loaded.

fields.name: quote_unit
fields.doc:
Display unit for the quote-denominated rows — native
`quoteConvertor.targetUnit`, i.e. `spot_makeQuoteCcyConvertor` →
`resolvedQuoteCcy`: `tradeQuoteCcy` (wire) → `instrument.displayQuoteCcy`
→ `instrument.quoteCcy` → the `instId` quote segment.

Used for the "(USDT)" suffix on Invested amount / Total PnL / Amount per
period / per-coin PnL titles (accessor A19). Empty when nothing resolves
— native renders `OKTSConstants.emptyDefaultString` ("--") in that case,
which the Swift side applies.

fields.name: charge_unit
fields.doc:
Display unit for the price-denominated rows — native
`chargeConvertor.quoteSymbol` (`spot_makePriceConvertor`). Drives the
"Average price (USDT)" title and the Parameters tab's "Quote currency of
order book" value (A19).

Tracked separately from [`Self::quote_unit`] on purpose: the charge
convertor and the quote convertor resolve through different instrument
fields and CAN differ (e.g. a `BTC-USD` instrument displayed as
`BTC-USDS` with `tradeQuoteCcy: USDC`). Native reads two different
convertors for these two rows; collapsing them into one field would be a
silent parity change.

fields.name: quote_precision
fields.doc:
Display precision for quote-denominated amounts — native
`quoteConvertor.targetUnitPrecision`, i.e.
`OKTBCoinPrecisionHelper.getCoinConfigPrecision(quoteUnit)`: the quote
coin's `sizeDig`, falling back to **2**.

Exposed because the Invest-More and Edit-Amount sheets take a
`quotePrecision:` argument that native derives from the convertor
(`param.quoteConvertor?.targetUnitPrecision ?? 2`). Without this field the
Rust arm would have to keep a convertor alive purely to recompute a value
the twins already resolved — a **dual-computed read**, which the
migration's definition of done does not permit waiving (unlike the
object-shaped `model:` argument those same sheets take).

Same resolver as the A1–A3 amount twins, so the sheet's precision and the
detail page's rendered amounts cannot disagree.

fields.name: profit_precision
fields.doc:
Display precision for PnL-denominated values — native
`profitConvertor?.precision ?? 4`, i.e. the instrument's index-config
`quote_dig` with the "no instrument ⇒ 4" fallback.

Exposed for the Overview **chart** sub-tab, whose VM reads
`profitConvertor?.precision ?? 4` directly
(`RecurringBuyDetailsOverviewChartViewModel.profitPrecision`). Without
this field that surface has to keep a convertor alive purely to recompute
the digit the Total-PnL twin already resolved — a dual-computed read,
which the definition of done does not permit waiving.

Same resolver as the A4a Total-PnL twin, so the chart's precision and the
rendered PnL cannot disagree.

fields.name: invested_amount_display
fields.doc:
A1 — Overview "Invested amount". Native:
`NSDecimalNumber.okt_(fromPlainString: investAmt)
.toLocalizedStringUp(toMax: getCoinConfigPrecision(quoteUnit))` →
**CEILING** at the quote coin's `sizeDig`, trailing zeros dropped, no
unit suffix (the unit lives in the row title).

fields.name: amount_per_period_display
fields.doc:
A2 — Overview "Amount per period". Same leaf as
[`Self::invested_amount_display`] but over `amt`, and **without** a
currency suffix.

fields.name: amount_per_period_with_unit_display
fields.doc:
A3 — **Parameters tab** "Amount per period". Identical number to
[`Self::amount_per_period_display`] but native appends the currency
(`.appendCurrency(ccy)`) on this row and not on the Overview one.

Kept as a separate field rather than reusing A2 + a Swift-side suffix so
the divergence is explicit and testable — the two rows genuinely differ
in native and a later session must not "unify" them.

fields.name: total_pnl_display
fields.doc:
A4a — Overview "Total PnL" amount half of the composite. Native
`OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.localizedPnl(withPnl:precision:)`: sign-dependent
truncation **toward zero** at the profit precision
(`plainPnlWithPnl` — negative `toPlainStringUpToMax`, positive
`toPlainStringDownToMax`), then an idempotent
`toLocalizedStringRoundToMax`, with "+" prepended on positives.
≡ `RoundingMode::Down` + `BotSignType::ExceptZero`, coloured by the raw
PnL sign.

The **composite** string (`"<pnl> (<ratio>)"`, reversed under RTL) is
assembled on the Swift side — it is a layout-direction concern
(`rtl_localizedStringWithProfit` branches on
`UIApplication.isLayoutRTL`), and joining two ICU-rendered numbers in
Rust would deny native its per-number `formatICUNumber` grouping pass.

fields.name: pnl_ratio_display
fields.doc:
A4b — Overview "Total PnL" ratio half. Native
`localizedPnlRatio(withPnlRatio:precision: 2)`: truncate toward zero,
`treatAsPercentage` (×100), `prependPlusSign`, then
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2` → **FLOOR, FIXED 2 dp (trailing zeros
KEPT), no clamp**.

⚠️ Deliberately built with `percent_display` (raw ratio, native applies
the ×100 + FLOOR at 2) and **not** with
`format_util::pnl_ratio_total_display`, which mirrors the Kotlin
`fmtPnlPercent` and applies a `MAX_PERCENT_VALUE` **clamp that iOS does
not have**. Reusing the Kotlin builder would diverge for tiny ratios.

fields.name: pnl_ratio_chart_color
fields.doc:
A17 — the Overview **chart header's** PnL-ratio colour direction.

A separate field from [`Self::pnl_ratio_display`]'s own colour because the
chart header applies a **different rule to the same raw ratio** — the
R-B20 shape again:

| | Overview cell (A4b) | Chart header (A17) |
|---|---|---|
| Native leaf | `localizedPnlRatio(…)` + `pnlColor` | `okts_isGreaterThanOrEqualToZero()` |
| Compare digit | 2 (truncate) | **4 (half-up)** |
| Zero | Neutral | **Up** (`>= 0` is Rise) |
| Blank / non-numeric | no colour | `contentPrimary` (a third colour) |

The compare digit differing from the *display* digit is the trap: a ratio
of `-0.00001` renders as `"0.00%"` but is still a Fall, and comparing at 2
would flip it to Rise.

`None` encodes native's `contentPrimary` early return — reached when
`localizedPnlRatio(…, precision: 2)` yields nothing renderable (blank or
non-numeric ratio). It is NOT "colour unknown": the Swift row must render
`contentPrimary` for `None`, not Rise. Native reference:
`RecurringBuyDetailsOverviewChartInfoViewState.swift:47-55`.

fields.name: triggered_times_display
fields.doc:
A6 — Parameters tab "Triggered recurring times". Native
`toLocalizedStringDown(toMax: 0)` → **FLOOR at 0 dp**.

Distinct from [`Self::cycles_display`] (A5), which formats the SAME
`cycles` value with the uncapped `toLocalizedString()` for the Overview
frequency line. Two twins over one raw field, because native uses two
different leaves.

fields.name: cycles_display
fields.doc:
A5 (rounds half) — the `{times}` slot of the Overview frequency line
(`"{frenquency}/{times}"`). Native `cycles.isEmpty ? "--" :
NSDecimalNumber.okt_(fromPlainString: cycles).toLocalizedString()` —
**no precision cap**, so the raw decimals pass through.

The localized `{frenquency}` half stays in Swift
(`RecurringBuyFrequencyFormatter`) — see the tracker's duplicate-check
list.

fields.name: next_purchase_visible
fields.doc:
A16 (guard half) — `false` when native renders "--" for "Next purchase":
the bot is paused **or** `nextInvestTime` is blank/non-numeric
(`getNextPurchaseText`: `if isPauseOrder || nextInvestmentTime.isEmpty`).

The date render itself stays native (`NSDate.fromTimestamp(ts / 1000)
.ok_string(… showUTC: true)`) — locale + timezone work with no
OKTradeCore type in its signature. Rust owns only the **predicate**, so
the pause-state comparison never needs an `OKTOrderStatusType` constant
on the Swift side.

Pause states pinned from `OKTTypes.m`: `"pause"` (:556) — native's guard
is `state == .pause` exactly, NOT the broader `pause|paused` pair the
action flags use.

fields.name: is_multi_currency
fields.doc:

Overview "Crypto | Target allocation" row (A7) and the multi-coin cell

fields.name: show_allocation_underline
fields.doc:

fields.name: aggregate_visible_count
fields.doc:
A9 — how many coins the multi-coin aggregate lines render before
truncating: native `createRecurringTextWithRecurringList` takes the FIRST
**2** entries when `count > 2`, else all of them.

Rust supplies the count + [`Self::aggregate_has_ellipsis`] rather than a
joined string, because the aggregate concatenates several *localised*
numbers: joining them in Rust would deny native its per-number
`formatICUNumber` grouping pass (the whole point of `BotDisplayText`).
Swift joins the per-coin twins with `", "` and appends `"..."`.

fields.name: aggregate_has_ellipsis
fields.doc: A9 — whether the aggregate line ends in `"..."` (native: `count > 2`).

fields.name: raw_json

like `algoOrdType` ⇄ `ordType`) gets the wire-shape keys it expects.
Building the model from the typed fields would silently drop the

bridge moves off MJExtension.

fields.name: load_more_error
fields.doc:
Load-more (pagination append) failure — SB-X03.

`error` alone could not serve pagination: it is cleared only when a
FIRST-PAGE fetch starts, so after a failed load-more the message survived
into the next successful load-more and a consumer that read `error` at the
load-more terminal reported the success as a failure. This field is cleared
when a load-more starts, so it always belongs to the attempt that just
finished.

Mirrors `BotEventHistoryState.load_more_error`, which had the pair from the
start. Additive: `#[uniffi(default = None)]` keeps every existing foreign
construction site compiling.

list is unchanged. Empty ≡ absent → fail-open to prior behavior. AC10.

name: bot_account_level
doc:
The account level, for analytics.

Replaces native `trade.tradeSetting.acctLv.rawValue ?? ""` — `OKTrade` is being
retired, and this read needed nothing from the instrument context it arrived through:
it is an account fact.

Returns `""` when unresolved, NOT core-trading's LEVEL_1 fallback.
[`get_account_level`](core_trading) coerces a missing config to `"1"`, which would make
analytics report a simple account for every event logged before the config lands —
fabricated data is worse than absent data for an analytics field, and native's `?? ""`
draws the same distinction. `is_account_level_resolved()` is the guard core-trading
provides for precisely this pairing.

Ungated, like the two digit resolvers below: this is an account-tier read that must not
silently become empty for a cohort, and `recurring_buy_place_order::resolve_recurring_identity`
already reads `Trade::instance()` directly for the same reason.

name: load_related_orders_in_time_window
doc:
Fetch the fills for one tapped position, native-iOS wire shape: BOTH
bounds are time params (`beforeTime` = the row's `c_time`, `after_time`
= its `u_time`) and `limit=100` is sent.

Deliberately a SEPARATE action rather than extra arguments on
`load_related_orders`: adding a parameter to an exported method breaks
every existing foreign call site, and this crate has no precedent for
`#[uniffi(default)]` on a method argument. Same reasoning as
`load_inst_tier` being separate from `refresh`.

The two shapes ask the server different questions — see
`related_orders_request`'s module doc. Results land on the same
`related_orders*` state fields, so only one may be in flight
(`SpawnPolicy::AlwaysCancel` on a shared effect key).

variants.doc: `symbol` holds a currency code — render it verbatim.

variants.doc: Contracts. `symbol` is EMPTY; native renders its own localized label.

variants.name: Lot
variants.doc: Lots (TradFi). `symbol` is EMPTY; native renders its own localized label.

doc:
What KIND of unit `symbol` denotes — because only a currency code is safe for
Rust to ship.

A currency code ("USDT", "BTC") is locale-invariant, so Rust supplies it and
native renders it verbatim. A contract or lot unit is a localized WORD
("zhang" / "Cont" / "Lot"), and `naming.md` forbids Rust producing user-facing
localized text — so for those Rust ships the kind and leaves `symbol` empty,
and native supplies its own localized label.

Discovered while wiring the detail page: `TradeUnit` (core-trading) has
`Coin` / `Contract` / `U` / `Lot`, and two of the four are not currency codes.

fields.name: positions_json

each kept position's raw JSON). Empty until the first seed/frame.

Retained for iOS, which parses `[OKTPosition]` from it verbatim. Android
reads the typed [`Self::positions`] instead — prefer that: the raw string
puts the wire contract for every position field on the native side, where
a server rename defaults silently rather than failing a typed decode.

fields.name: positions

fields.name: total_pnl_display
fields.doc:
Total PnL (`totalPnlWithRatioItem`'s value half): `getBotPnl(totalPnl,
isShowSymbol = true)`. **On the STOPPED/HISTORY arm this struct covers,
its `.color` is the ONE combined color for the whole row** — legacy's
`StrategyHistoryListResp` branch applies a single `tvColor`
(`getPnlColor(getDigitPnl(totalPnl))`, colored on the ROUNDED value) to
the concatenated `"$totalProfit ($ratio)"` text, and
[`pnl_ratio_display`]'s own `.color` is unused here — do not wire it to
anything on THIS arm. This does NOT generalize to the RUNNING/PENDING
arm: its own standalone `ratioItem` IS independently colored via
`getPnlColor(fmtBotDigitPnlPercent(pnlRatio))`
(`TacticListDataMapper.kt:2331-2337`) — the exact precision-only color
[`pnl_ratio_display`] already carries — so a future running-arm port
can and should reuse this same field's color for that row.

fields.name: pnl_ratio_display
fields.doc:

[`total_pnl_display`] for the arm-scoped color note.

one `tvColor` comes from the RAW `arbitragePnl`, already carried by
`arb_profit_display`, not from this rate).

fields.name: arbitrage_apr_display

arbitrageApy)`) — independent of [`total_apr_display`]'s color.

fields.name: total_apr_display

totalApy)`).

(`TacticListDataMapper.kt:4275-4279`). Plain `String`, not

and a currency code is a label, not a number.

doc:
Contract DCA Overview field-grid display group for the STOPPED/HISTORY arm
of `TacticListDataMapper`'s Contract DCA branch (`data is
StrategyHistoryListResp`, `:4247-4388`). One cohesive Record per R26e
rather than appending another ~7 loose `*_display` fields onto
[`ContractDcaBotInfo`] directly (the 2026-09-10 History-summary-card
addition already did that once and the standard asks not to repeat it).

Mirrors `spot_dca/detail.rs::apply_dca_field_grid_displays` field-for-field

`symbol = data.getInvestmentccy()` and no other candidate, unlike Spot
DCA's `invest_symbol = price_symbol.ifBlank(investmentCcy)`).

The RUNNING/PENDING arm is a separate, larger port (6 distinct ordered
lists, 19 item objects) and is NOT covered here — see the slice manifest's
"Scoped follow-up: Overview field grid".

name: fetch_min_investment
doc:
Fetch the minimum investment for the CURRENT basket.

The basket is read from this state, not passed in. It used to be a parameter, and
iOS built it from the ObjB mirror — the copy of the basket that lags Rust by two
async hops and cannot represent emptiness — with
`String(format: "%f", Double(rate) / 100.0)`, a float round-trip on a ratio that
`money_math.md` forbids and that spelled 33% as `"0.330000"` where
`ratio_percent_to_wire` spells it `"0.33"`. So the minimum could be computed for a
different basket than the one that would be ordered.

`invest_ccy` stays a parameter on purpose. It is `recurringItem.orderUnit`, which
native has from the instrument before this state does — `set_invest_ccy` is written
by the page's own sync — so deriving it here would send `""` in the window before
that lands.

No request is issued for an empty basket: there is no minimum for buying nothing,
and the endpoint would be asked to price an empty list.

name: bot_voucher_pnl_display
doc:
Bridge `BotDataUtil.getPnl` for the Smart Arbitrage Overview's voucher
amount formatter (`SmartArbitrageOverviewFragment::buildVoucherAmountFormatter`,
`VoucherInfoUiMapper.AmountFormatter`). Returns the SAME
`pnl_total_display`-family (`format_util.rs`, migration #76) ICU-ready
value legacy computes, plus the unit legacy appends, so the Kotlin caller
only runs the existing `BotDisplayTextRenderer` render + unit concat —
never recomputes precision.

legacy's `getSymbol(isQuoteCcy = true)` DISCARDS the passed `mSymbol`/`unit`
whenever `inst_id` is non-blank, re-deriving from
`getSuggestedInstrument(instType, instId)?.getQuoteSymbol()` for BOTH the
coin-size-digit lookup and (via `getDisplayQuoteSymbol()`) the appended
unit; `unit` is load-bearing ONLY on legacy's `instId.isBlank() -> this`
branch. Mirrored 1:1 here: when `inst_id` is blank, `unit` becomes both the
precision-lookup symbol and the returned unit — a divergent `unit` can
never silently outrank the bot's own instrument when one is resolvable.

`with_sign` mirrors legacy's `isShowSymbol`: `true` -> `EXCEPT_ZERO` ("+"
only for `pnl > 0`, the accumulated-interest case); `false` -> `AUTO` (no
"+", the loss-payment case).

`None` = gate off / blank `pnl` / unresolvable symbol / non-numeric `pnl`
-> caller renders `NO_VALUE_PLACE_HOLDER`, matching legacy's own
`symbol.isNullOrEmpty() || pnl.isEmpty()` short-circuit. No silent
0-precision or empty-unit fallback.

fields.name: account_id
fields.doc:
Sub-account id that owns this bot (wire `accountId`). The V2 bot K-line
derives its buy/sell-point `sid` from this: a non-empty, non-zero value
enables the chart's bot buy/sell-point scope, while empty leaves it
disabled exactly as legacy does. `StrategyDetailsResponse.accountId` is a
nullable Long the server sends either bare (`478`) or quoted (`"478"`) on
the shared `/priapi/v5/algo/trade/info` payload; `deserialize_string_or_number`
normalizes both to a `String`, yielding `""` when the wire omits it or
sends `null`, and `"0"` for a literal zero (which the K-line treats as
no-scope). Same wire key and semantics as `SpotGridBotInfo` /
`BotIdentity.account_id` (`wire_scalar_string(snapshot, "accountId")`),
`ContractGridBotInfo.account_id`, and smart arbitrage. Appended last so the
UniFFI Record field order of the existing fields stays stable; the
`#[uniffi(default = "")]` keeps existing native initializers
source-compatible.

name: PrivateModeInfo
doc:
Public domain model for the `private-mode/info` response.

**Promoted to the FFI surface** (2026-07-18): the native re-wire PR
(iOS + Android delete their ObjC/Kotlin request centers and call
`OKTSPrivateCopyService` instead) is queued, so per
`docs/conventions/public_types.md § promote-on-demand` this now carries
`#[derive(uniffi::Record)]` and crosses the FFI boundary as a Swift struct /
Kotlin data class. The DTO `PrivateModeInfoResponse`
(`src/types/private_copy/private_mode_info.rs`) produces it via
`into_domain(self)`; `OKTSPrivateCopyService::fetch_private_mode_info` returns it.

`private_mode` is a bare `bool` (defaults `false`). The three count fields
are `Option<String>` because the server sends them as strings-or-null and
the absence is UI-meaningful (native distinguishes "no quota data yet"
from a real value). They stay `String` (not numeric) — display strings,
not order-affecting quantities.

name: place_order
doc:
Submit the order using the current state. Short-circuits to
`place_order_state = Error` with raw English key when:
- `inst_id` is empty → `"instrument_required"`
- `sz` is empty → `"order_size_required"`

There is deliberately NO ccy gate: native's ccy requirement is a
debug-only `NSAssert` scoped to margin biz
(`OKTSmartIcebergStgyPORootVC.m:298-302`) — release native submits
without `ccy` and lets the backend adjudicate. A runtime gate here
blocked every spot submit (`td_mode` seeds `"cross"`, iOS pushes no
ccy — IB-014).

Otherwise spawns the place-order effect with
`SpawnPolicy::AlwaysCancel` so back-to-back submits cancel the
prior in-flight request (mirrors `[self.placeOrderLoader cancel]`
at `OKTSmartIcebergStgyPORootVC.m:325`).

SB-A18a. Native `calculateFiledAmount`
(`OKTSSignalBotDetailCurrentOrderCellViewModel.m:154-165`):

where `precision` is the quote coin's config precision.

use `.round`) — that asymmetry is native's and is reproduced here rather
than normalised. Emitted PRE-SCALED so the renderer's fixed FLOOR cannot
undo it, the same technique `contract_grid_slippage_display` uses.

new wire field. Any missing/unparseable input ⇒ `Placeholder`, matching
native's `accFillPlainAmount` returning `""`.

name: arb_price_type_choices
doc:
The price-type chips a leg offers, in native's order.

**Order is load-bearing.** Native's grid reports the tapped chip by INDEX and
the VC resolves it as `priceGroupDatas[selectIndex]`
(`OKTASPOPriceGridVC.m:actionBBOSelectItem:`), so reordering this list
silently remaps every tap. The order is queuing → over-price → BBO → market,
which is neither alphabetical nor the order the constants are declared in.

`is_option_biz` disables **market price only** — options reject market orders
for arbitrage. Every other chip is unconditionally supported.

Manual entry (`enter`) is deliberately absent: it is not a chip. It is the
state the grid falls back to when no chip is selected, which is why
`arb_price_type_title` has no branch for it either.

doc:
Native `getTradeDataSettings()?.fetchMtkCloseAllConfirm()` — whether closing a
position at market asks for a second confirmation.

The cold-cache default matches native and was verified, not assumed:
`TradeConfigInfoProvider.fetchMtkCloseAllConfirm()` is
