`BigSafeDecimal`, so an absent config compares `0 == 1` => FALSE. core-trading's
getter is `.unwrap_or(false)` for the same case, so both arms skip the dialog
on a cold cache. Do NOT "fix" this to default true — that would add a
confirmation legacy does not show.

name: smart_iceberg_position_pnl_display
doc:
Row 4 — unrealised PnL (`upl`) through the position **profit** convertor
([`profit_spec`]), rounded [`RoundingMode::Down`] (native `.down` ==
`NSRoundDown` == toward zero). `upl` is signed, so this is NOT
[`RoundingMode::Floor`]: a loss of `-1.375` at 2 dp shows `-1.37`, not
`-1.38`.

`ccy` is the position's `stgyMgnCcy`. The convertor's symbol rides inline.

⚠️ **The color is computed from the RAW `upl` string, not from the rounded
display value** (`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:205-211`). A PnL of
`-0.0000001` at precision 4 renders `"0"` but is still colored FALL. This is
the opposite of row 5, which colors the ROUNDED value — the asymmetry is
native's and both halves are copied.

name: SignalBotOrderExtra
doc:
The Android order card's side tag plus its reduce-only row value — the two
projections that are Android-shaped and therefore must not join the shared
`SignalBotOrderDisplay`.

`side_label_key` is a localization key, or **EMPTY** for native's
unknown-`instType` fallback. Empty is a legitimate value here, not a failure:
native's `else -> "" to false` arm renders an **empty label with FALL
colours**, not a hidden tag. Kotlin must therefore resolve a non-empty key or
fail the batch, and pass an empty one straight through.

Deliberately NOT a [`SignalBotDisplayUnit`]: that type's Kotlin `render()`
goes through `CtString.resolve()` -> `CtStringResourceCache`, a five-key
hardcoded map whose miss path returns `""`. Only the two amount-unit keys are
registered there, so a new key routed through it would resolve blank, trip the
`unit_unresolved` guard and silently fall the whole batch back to native. That
is exactly how signal bot's `headerStatus` shipped inert. These keys are
resolved by a LOCAL map in the bot repo that fails loudly instead.

name: submit_leg
doc:
Submit a single leg.

Per the ObjC oracle (`OKTASPOContentVC.getOrderCommitParams`, m:876-884)
a per-leg submit forces `major = "true"` **regardless of which leg it
is**, and forces `associate = "false"` — the server rejects a
single-entry `instList` that claims association. Both overrides are
applied here, not by the caller.

name: set_amount_from_percent

margin_precision)`, sets it as `input_amt`, and records the endpoint's
fractional `input_percent` so [`Self::submit`] forwards `50%` as `0.5`.
Values outside `1..=100` clear the input.

name: replace_with_ws_data
doc:
Replace with the authoritative instrument-list snapshot. BOTH platforms.

`SignalBotPositionInstIdsTask.updateWsOrder` has already rebuilt this
list in remote order and applied its Native cache rule before invoking
the bridge. Reapplying a second Rust cache here would diverge from the
exact snapshot the gate-OFF Fragment receives. Empty clears the tab.

No longer gated to `cfg(any(test, target_os = "android"))`, because iOS
has the identical need: native's membership channel
(`processInstIdsWSResult:`, `OKTSSignalBotPositionLiveDataSource.m:212-238`)
rebuilds the list in the frame's order while REUSING each row it already
holds, and only falls back to the frame's row for an instId it has never
seen. That "keep the richer row, follow the frame's membership" result is
a full list, so it has to arrive through a replace — pushing the frame's
leaner rows through the merge entry would overwrite live values instead.
iOS computes that list on its side and hands the finished snapshot here,
which is the same division of labour Android already uses.

fields.name: signal_count
fields.doc:
`signalCount` — how many times this signal has FIRED.

A DIFFERENT wire field from `symbols_number`, and the two are easy to
confuse: native declares both on `OKTStgyInfoModel` — `symbolsNumber`
(`.h:535`, "Full currency pair count") and `signalCount` (`.h:593`,
"Signal trigger count"). Lifted here because the iOS Rust arm had no
field for it and was passing `symbols_number` in its place, so the share
card's "Signal trigger count" row rendered the pair count
(`OKTSOrderListUtil.m:1161-1162`). That row is the ONLY surface for this
value — the detail page itself never shows it, which is why the
substitution went unnoticed.

DECLARED LAST, and that position is load-bearing. Field order IS the
FFI contract: the generated Kotlin constructor is positional, so a
defaulted field only spares an existing call site if every
non-defaulted field still sits at the index that site passes. This
field first landed between `symbols_number` and `win_rate`, which left
`max_drawdown` unfilled for every Kotlin site passing the pre-MR
argument list — and adding the default there would NOT have fixed that,
because the shifted list still runs one argument short. Appending after
the whole defaulted block is what actually keeps those sites compiling.
Do not sort this back up next to `symbols_number` for readability.

name: place_order_from_state
doc:
Submit the order using the basket Rust already owns.

Prefer this over [`Self::place_order_with_coins`], which takes the
coin list as an argument. Refuses a basket that
`is_coin_allocation_valid` rejects, so a native call site that
missed a disabled Confirm cannot post ratios the server will bounce.
Submit the order Rust already holds. Returns whether it was ACCEPTED.

`false` means it was refused locally and no effect was spawned, so no
result and no error will follow — the caller must undo whatever it did in
anticipation (native shows a loading HUD before calling, and that HUD is
dismissed by the result/error sinks, so a silent refusal would leave it
spinning forever). This return value is the whole reason the refusal is
safe to have: native has its own inline allocation error and normally
blocks first, but the two checks read different copies of the basket —
native reads the ObjC mirror, which is a MainActor hop behind and can be
a strict SUBSET of Rust's (`mirrorRustBasketIntoItem` skips a ccy it
cannot resolve and bails on an empty result) — so they can disagree.

name: create
doc:
Construct a `StopBotInteractor` with an injected stop service.

The interactor is fully bot-agnostic — native obtains the
bot-common stop service from
`OKTSBotCommonService::bot_stop_service()` and passes the
resulting handle in. Mirrors the
`Arc<BotRenameActionServiceHandle>` constructor-injection
pattern that `RenameBotInteractor::create` uses.

```ignore
let handle = OKTSBotCommonService::new().bot_stop_service();
let interactor = StopBotInteractor::create(algo_id, inst_id, bot_type, handle);
```

# Arguments
* `algo_id` — Bot algorithm ID
* `inst_id` — Instrument ID (e.g. `"BTC-USDT"`)
* `bot_type` — Bot type (SpotGrid, ContractGrid, SpotDCA,
ContractDCA)
* `stop_service_handle` — FFI handle wrapping
`Arc<dyn BotStopServiceTrait>`, obtained from the bot-common
facade.

instrument, and the bot-pool `algo_id` endpoint this used to call

name: resolve_smart_arb_route_inst_family
doc:
Resolve the inst family for an arbitrary (`inst_type`, `inst_id`) route pair — used only to
route a deep-link entry to the matching `FundingRateArbCoin` recommendation BEFORE any coin
is selected. `SmartArbitragePlaceOrderState::inst_family` resolves the currently SELECTED
coin's identity; this resolves an unselected candidate for routing only, so it isn't a state
field. `""` when unresolved (blank id, cold store, unknown instrument), same convention as
`SmartArbReducePositionsIdentity`.

name: format_grid_profit_text
doc:
G7 — grid profit-text COMPOSITE. Returns the PARTS (not the assembled string).

Replicates legacy `buildGridProfitText` (StrategyConvert.kt:421-491), whose
amounts route through `getBotPnl(isShowUnit = false, isShowSymbol = false)` →
`getBotPrecision` and whose blank-decision routes through `getDigitPnl`. The
two legacy precisions are NOT the same and must be modeled separately:

* **Displayed amount** (`getBotPnl` → `getBotPrecision`,
StrategyConvert.kt:279-305): precision = `max(pairDigit, currencyDigit)`
where `pairDigit = getPnlPrecision(instId, instType)` = the SPOT
`createProfitConverterWithIndex` `quote_dig` (`resolve_profit_digit`,
fallback 0) and `currencyDigit = getTradeCoinInfo(unit)?.sizeDig`
(`resolve_get_bot_precision_coin_digit`, **fallback 0 — no 4**). Per-sign
DOWN(>0)/UP(≤0), drop zeros, AUTO sign, no `+`, no color.
* **Blank decision** (`getDigitPnl`, StrategyConvert.kt:373-398):
`digit = max(currencyDigit, pairDigit)`, then `if digit == 0 →
RECURRING_DEFAULT_DIGIT(4)`, per-sign rounding; `isAmtBlank` is
`getDigitPnl(min).eq("0") || getDigitPnl(max).eq("0")`. The `4` floor here
only bites when BOTH `quote_dig` and the coin `sizeDig` are absent.

`unit` is the legacy `getPnlUnit(instId, instType, profit_ccy)`; for the SPOT
create flow that resolves to `profit_ccy` (the quote ccy) — passed through
directly. `inst_type` is part of the legacy signature, kept for a 1:1 native
call shape; the SPOT digit sources key on the inst id / ccy (SPOT inst family
== inst id).

name: RecurringSearchCoin

fields.name: inst_id
fields.doc:
The spot instrument id, `<base>-<quote>`. Native used it only to ask for
the countdown model; it is carried anyway because the caller keys its
per-coin price range on the same string.

fields.name: base_ccy
fields.doc:
RAW, case-sensitive base currency — `XQQQ`, never the `xQQQ` display form.
This is the DATA key: icon lookups, dedupe, and the deeplink match all use
it, and folding case here would break the xStock pairs.

fields.name: display_base_ccy
fields.doc:
The UI label — `xQQQ` for an xStock pair, otherwise identical to
[`Self::base_ccy`]. Native's `displayBaseCcy ?: baseCcy` ladder is already
applied, so the caller must not repeat it.

fields.name: coin_full_name
fields.doc:
The coin's full name (the wire `coinName`), native's `coinFullName`.

Note for anyone tracing this back into core-trading: the accessor is
`full_coin_name()`. The similarly-named `get_coin_full_name()` returns the
BASE CCY, not the name, so reading the obvious one gives a coin whose
title is its own symbol.

fields.name: is_waiting_online
fields.doc:
Listed but not yet tradable — the search list shows these rows and refuses
to select them, and the seeding pass skips them.

Derived from the instrument's `bizStatus`, NOT from native's separate
countdown store. That is a deliberate, documented difference: core-trading
treats `bizStatus` as the authoritative gate (its own
`new_coin_count_down_use_case` says so, with the countdown model as
optional detail), and the store native reads
(`OKTrade.instCountDownDataManager`) is not reachable from Rust. Residual
skew: the two are fed by different channels, so around the instant a coin
goes live one may flip before the other.

fields.name: registry_name
fields.doc:
The coin REGISTRY's display name, e.g. `bitcoin`.

Not a duplicate of [`Self::coin_full_name`], and the two must not be
substituted for one another. That one is the INSTRUMENT's `coinName`; this is
`TradeCoinInfo.name` out of `public/coins`. Native read them at different call
sites from different objects — the search list from the instrument, the picker
sheet from `coinsBySymbol[symbol].name` — so both are carried rather than one
being assumed to stand in for the other. They may well hold the same text;
that is not the same as being the same field.

Empty when the registry has no entry for this coin.

fields.name: groups
fields.doc:
Trading-zone ids from the coin registry. Empty for a coin in no zone, and also
empty when the registry has no entry — the picker's own `?? []` covered both.

fields.name: list_time
fields.doc:
The INSTRUMENT's listing time, as the wire string. Native
`instrument.listTime ?? ""`.

The instrument's, not the registry's: `TradeCoinInfo` also carries a
`list_time` and it is a different field. Reached by matching
`Instrument::Spot` — `BizInstrument` exposes no accessor for it.

fields.name: icon_url
fields.doc:
The coin registry's icon url, or EMPTY when the registry has none.

Empty is a real, expected outcome rather than an error, and the caller
MUST handle it: native's `imageURLForCoin:` synthesizes a CDN url from
`OKFResourceAcceleratorManager` when the registry misses, which is exactly
the case for a coin that is listed but absent from `public/coins` — i.e.
the [`Self::is_waiting_online`] rows. That synthesis needs platform
configuration Rust has no access to, so it stays native. The split is
deliberate: the DATA (registry url) comes from here, the PLATFORM CONFIG
(CDN domain) stays where it is owned, and neither needs `OKTrade`.

doc:
One coin the recurring-buy search list may offer for a given quote currency.

Field-for-field what the native loop set on its `OKTRecurringCoin`:

| native | here |
|---|---|
| `instrument.coinFullName` -> MJ `name` | `coin_full_name` |
| `instrument.baseCcy` -> MJ `symbol` (also re-set explicitly) | `base_ccy` |
| `instrument.displayBaseCcy ?: baseCcy` -> MJ `displaySymbol` | `display_base_ccy` |
| `trade.countDownModel(withInstID:) != nil` | `is_waiting_online` |
| `trade.okts_imageURL(forCoin: symbol)` | `icon_url` (see the field doc) |

variants.name: Instant
variants.doc:

Start Condition row renders the localized "Trigger Immediately" label
(`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:164-165`). No tap affordance.

variants.name: Price
variants.doc:
Wire `"price"` — native `isIndicatorPrice`.
Row renders `<localized Price Trigger> | <formatted trigger_px>`
(`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:166-170`); tapping opens the price
detail alert (`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:190-198`).

variants.name: Rsi

(`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:171-172`); tapping opens the RSI detail

variants.name: Unsupported
variants.doc:
Anything else: the wire literals this screen does not handle
(`"webhook"`, `"end_round_stop"`), an empty/absent indicator pair, or
a future literal.

**This is behaviour, not an error arm.** All four cases make native's
three `isIndicator*` predicates return `NO`, the row's `value` stays
nil, and the VC renders `--`; `showStartConditionBtn`
(`OKTSmartIcebergInfoVC.m:348-361`) also returns `NO`, so there is no
tap affordance. Native reaches the same place when the whole
start-trigger entry is missing — see `SmartIcebergStgyInfo.start_trigger`.

doc:
Resolved start-trigger indicator — the Rust port of native's three
`isIndicator*` predicates on `OKTSOrderSignParamsModel`.

**Why an enum and not the two raw wire strings.** Native resolves the
indicator from *two* fields with a precedence rule
(`OKTSOrderSignParamsModel.m:84-112`): `indicator` wins whenever it is
non-empty, and only when it is empty does `triggerStrategy` get a say —
the header at `:70` notes `indicator` "will gradually be replaced by
triggerStrategy", so both are live on the wire today. Every one of the
three predicates repeats that same ladder verbatim. Exporting the two raw
strings would make each native platform re-derive the ladder, and getting
the precedence backwards silently renders `--` instead of the real row.
Rust resolves once; Swift/Kotlin match on the result.

name: seed_info_from_entry
doc:
Seed `info` from the bot-list ENTRY payload, before the detail fetch
lands, so the Overview card renders at its real height on first frame
instead of growing from zero when the first HTTP push arrives.

`json` is the raw wire row the bot list already holds for this bot
(`OKTSHoardCoinOrderModel`). It is parsed with the SAME
`SmartPortfolioStrategyInfoResponse` DTO and run through the SAME
`into_domain()` as the HTTP response, so the display twins come out of
one formatter and the seed cannot drift from the fetched render. That
single-funnel property is the whole reason the seed crosses into Rust
rather than being formatted natively.

Deliberately narrow — it writes `info` and NOTHING else:

1. **`info_json` stays `None`.** That field is the WS merge base, and
`apply_ws_update` drops a partial frame when there is no base (see the
invariant on that fn). The entry row carries FEWER fields than the
detail payload, so promoting it to the merge base would let a delta
merge onto an incomplete base — the defect that invariant exists to
prevent.
2. **`info_state` is untouched.** The screen gates success / no-data /
error rendering on it; a seed is not a fetch result.
3. **An existing `info` is never overwritten.** Fetched data must not be
downgraded to a seed, and a second seed call is a no-op.
4. **An unusable payload changes no state** — never blank what is there.
That covers both a hard parse failure AND a payload that deserializes
without being an entry row: every DTO field is `#[serde(default)]` and
`serde` accepts a sequence for a struct, so `"[]"` / `"{}"` would
otherwise seed an all-empty record whose twins are every
`Placeholder` — a fully-populated `--` header. A non-empty `algoId` is
the entry-row test.

`order_status` is left alone too: it is driven by the fetch / WS paths.

name: resync_coins_for_quote_ccy
doc:
Re-align the basket with a new quote currency.

Drops assets that are not tradable in `quote_ccy`, then seeds one if the basket is
empty afterwards — which includes having been empty on entry. Survivors keep their price
bounds, and their ratios follow native `OKTRecurringItem.removeSelectedCoin:`
exactly: an EVEN basket is re-split over the survivors, an uneven one keeps its
ratios and leaves the deficit visible rather than silently reshaping the user's
split.

This doc used to say the ratios were never rebalanced, "same rule as
`remove_coin`" — wrong twice over, since that method DID rebalance an even basket
and so does native. `remove_coin` itself is gone now; `retain_coins_in_universe`
is the only implementation of the rule.

`fallback_universe` is the eligible base currencies NATIVE computed for
`quote_ccy`, used only when this crate's own read comes back empty. That read is
`bot_recurring_seed_universe`, which opens with `if !ct_enabled { return
Vec::new() }` — so for the core-trading control cohort it is ALWAYS empty and this
method could never prune anything. Rust's basket then kept assets that are not
tradable in the new currency, permanently: `set_coins` has no universe gate, so a
picker selection lands whatever it is given and nothing can ever remove it again.
Native has the universe on either cohort (it walks OKTrade's instrument store), so
it hands it over rather than the alternative — reconciling two baskets in Swift,
which took three attempts and broke something each time.

Pass it EMPTY to keep the old behaviour: no prune, and no reseed, when this crate
cannot see the instruments.

The trailing reseed uses the SAME resolved universe — it must, or a prune from the
fallback could empty a basket the reseed then cannot refill. Callers therefore need
to hand over a list that means "listed AND tradable", matching what this crate's own
read returns; native filters its not-yet-live instruments before passing it.
`seed_default_coin` is unaffected and still reads only this crate's own universe.

name: recurring_coin_info_warmed
doc:
[`recurring_coin_info`], but it WAITS for the coin registry first.

For callers that are not preceded by a warm-up. The synchronous read answers
`None` on a cold store and does not prime it, which is safe on the place-order
page — its `performNativeSetup` awaits `recurring_search_universe`, so the
store is warm by the time anything reads it — and was NOT safe on the
order-detail action sheets. Reached from the running-bots list nothing primes this
store — a strategy detail does, but only on the Rust cohort — so `coinId` came back nil and
the Edit-amount / Invest-more sheets refused to build at all: a dead button
with no feedback. That shipped (iOS `fb646c0b4`).

## What the await buys, and what it does NOT

It removes the ORDERING race: this caller no longer reads before the load
that primes the store. It does NOT promise the store is populated
afterwards. `ensure_trade_data_loaded` returns `()` and swallows every error
it meets — four sites in `trade_data_preload.rs`, by design, because "a load
failure must NOT abort the bot-info fetch". Offline, a `/coins` 5xx, or a
`NoDataFound` all leave the registry cold and this function still answers
`None`.

So `None` means "unknown coin OR the warm-up could not complete". A caller
must degrade the one value that needed it and must NOT tell the user (or a
log reader) that the currency does not exist — it cannot know that.

## Cost: treat it as a network call

Not a completed future on the first call. `ensure_coins_loaded` keys off a
login-state marker initialised to `-1`, so the first call in a process always
takes the forced branch and awaits a `/coins` round trip, and `load_spot_biz`
can add `/simpleProduct` + `/config`. By this function's own premise its
callers ARE that first caller, so give it a loading state.

## Why a second export rather than reusing the exported warm-up

iOS awaiting the already-exported `ensure_bot_trade_data_loaded` and then
calling the synchronous read would need no new export — but that one is gated
on `use_core_trading_rust()`, so it would no-op for the control cohort and
leave the dead button live there. This awaits the UNGATED
`ensure_trade_data_loaded` instead, so both cohorts warm. The gate difference
is deliberate: do not "restore" it by following that precedent, which is a
precedent for the cancellation SHAPE only.

A cancelled call yields `None`. Neither shipped iOS caller retains the token
it constructs, so neither can currently cancel.

name: smart_iceberg_is_open_close_mode
doc:
Whether the Positions tab shows the "available to close" row — native gates
it on the account's position mode being open/close (long_short), i.e.
`Trade::instance().trade_setting().is_open_close_mode()`
(`core-trading/src/core/trade/manager/account_config_getter.rs:776-779`).

**A LIVE read, deliberately un-memoized.** The position mode is a user
setting that can change while the Detail screen is open; a value cached on
either side of the FFI would keep the row visible (or hidden) until the next
parse. Swift calls this per render, exactly like the value funnels.

⚠️ On a COLD account config this returns `true` — `get_position_mode()`
defaults to `DOUBLE_POSITION_MODE` when no config is loaded
(`account_config_getter.rs:389-393`). That is native's own default, so a
cold read is faithful rather than a bug; the positions flow additionally
awaits `Trade::trade_setting_future()` at its fetch choke point
(`interactors/smart_iceberg/positions_live.rs`) so the window is short.

name: save_trade_config
doc:
Write the trade-config from the price-settings sheet, then republish the
server's echo into state.

Replaces the iOS `OKTRequestCenter.setArbTradeConfig:` call. Two rules the
caller does NOT have to reimplement: the blank-input fallback to the
currently stored interval / threshold (native's "per backend requirements"
comment), and the `[1, 50]` bounds gate — the action refuses out-of-range
input with `ActionResultState::Error` instead of writing it, so a caller
that skips the pre-submit check still cannot push a bad value.

On success the echoed config overwrites the same fields
`load_trade_config` writes, and every derived price is recomputed because
the taker / maker ranges feed the over-price and queuing branches.

name: smart_iceberg_price_display_plain
doc:
Row 6 — "Maker Price Limit" (`pxLimit`): the legacy
`[[chargeConv toQuoteFormated:pxLimit].round toPlainString]` leaf
(`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:158-160`) — quote-convert, truncate at the
convertor's `quotePrecision` with `NSRoundPlain`, then render **without**
locale grouping.

Returns `Raw` on the SUCCESS path, deliberately: `Raw` is the only
`BotDisplayText` variant native renders verbatim, and `toPlainString` is
documented as the ungrouped render. Every other numeric funnel in this
module returns `Number` / `Wrapped` precisely because its legacy leaf DOES
group. The consequence is that a success value and a parse-failure
passthrough share the `Raw` variant here — that is the honest encoding of
"native shows the string as-is either way", and it is asserted in
[`tests::maker_price_limit_row_diverges_from_the_grouped_price_rows`].

**Per-row divergence on the unit:** native blanks the row's `suffixText`
(`@""`) when `pxLimit` is empty rather than showing the quote symbol, so the
Swift caller must skip [`smart_iceberg_quote_symbol`] on the blank branch.
The value itself still degrades to `Placeholder` (native renders `"--"`),
matching every other funnel here.

fields.name: load_state

Lifecycle of the `fetch_profits` GET, mirroring the `load_state` /
`withdraw_state` split in the sibling `spot_grid::withdraw_profit`
interactor. Authoritative answer to "has the profits GET completed"
— `action_state` cannot serve this because its `Idle` is ambiguous
by construction (see its doc comment below). Native's
`applyRustState` must branch on `load_state`, not `action_state`,
to decide whether the four rows are ready to render.
`Option` + `default = None` rather than a bare `#[uniffi(default)]`: the vendored
bindgen cannot render a bare default for an enum-typed field (it bails with
"Invalid literal for enum type"), and the `uniffi` macro parses only literals, so an
`ActionResultState::Idle` default cannot be expressed either. `Option` + `None` is the
precedented additive shape — see `live`'s `TokenToPromote::tag_kind` and `planet`'s
`feed_models.rs`. `None` means "no profits GET has been attempted", which is exactly
the pre-fetch state, so the nullability carries real meaning rather than being noise.

name: apply_recommendation
doc:
Apply a handed-over recommendation plan in ONE mutation.

The AI tab's "Set custom parameters" lands here. Atomic on purpose: doing
it through `set_coins` plus `set_coin_ratios` plus a setter per schedule
field publishes a state per call, and the ones in between carry the
picker's default split rather than the recommended one — so the form would
visibly reshape itself on the way to the plan the user actually chose.
`smart_portfolio_place_order::reset_form` takes its coins for the same
reason.

Ratios arrive as the wire's decimal fractions and are converted here, not
by the caller: the conversion is money math (`Decimal`, round DOWN, per
native `OKTSRecurringBuyPOParam.m:63`) and belongs on this side of the FFI.
A coin whose ratio does not parse is DROPPED rather than seeded at 0% — a
0% coin looks selected and contributes nothing.

REFUSES the whole plan — no field written, `recommend_id` included — when that
leaves no installable coin, i.e. the plan carried no assets or every ratio
failed to parse. The basket is assigned wholesale here, and an empty Rust
basket cannot propagate to the ObjC item that still draws the iOS screen
(the mirror drops empty; `updateCoins:` early-returns on an empty array), so
applying it would leave a complete-looking 100% form over a basket that
submission refuses. Leaving both copies on the previous plan keeps them
agreeing; the refusal is logged.

Returns whether the plan was installed. `false` is the refusal above, and it
is not advisory: a native caller that also writes the form itself — iOS's copy
path writes the schedule through notifying `OKTRecurringItem` setters, which
reach this state — must skip those writes, or the plan lands half-applied,
which is the divergence this atomic apply exists to prevent.

name: ContractGridBotInfo

fields.name: ord_type
fields.doc:
Wire key `algoOrdType` — explicit `serde(rename)`, NOT `rename_all`.

The payload carries BOTH `ordType` and `algoOrdType` with the same
value (verified by packet capture), so `rename_all`'s implicit
`ordType` did parse; the rename pins the CANONICAL key — the one iOS
native reads (`OKTStgyInfoModel`'s mj mapping
`@"ordType" : @"algoOrdType"`, OKTStgyInfoModel.m:37) — instead of the
duplicate, so a server that ever drops the legacy alias cannot silently
blank this field.

Do NOT reach for `#[serde(alias = "ordType")]`: serde derive treats an
alias and the canonical name as the SAME field, and a payload carrying
both raises a duplicate-field error that would fail the whole detail
parse. The struct has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so the unread duplicate
key is simply ignored.

The FIELD name stays `ord_type` for Kotlin ABI compatibility: the
Android trading-bot binary already calls the generated
`ContractGridBotInfo.getOrdType()`
(`ContractGridOverviewPatchMappingKt.patchWithRust`); renaming the
field renames that getter and fails the Android refer-check
(pipeline 13259441). Do NOT rename to `algo_ord_type`.
`default` matters here: without it `algoOrdType` is a REQUIRED key and
a server that dropped it would fail the ENTIRE detail parse, not just
blank this one row. Every sibling field in this struct carries it.

fields.name: rule_type
fields.doc:
Instrument rule type (server field `ruleType`). Feeds the title
formatter's raw-instId vs display-id decision (`getCoinTitle`), which

fields.name: is_history
fields.doc:
RAW wire `isHistory` (`StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:279`).

Deliberately kept separate from the derived history axis: the two have
DIFFERENT predicates and are NOT interchangeable. The Overview row set
switches on `state == "stopped" || isHistory`
(`TacticListDetailsDataMapper.kt:927`), but the About block's
"Stopped time" row gates on this raw field ALONE —
`if (botDetailResp.isHistory) botDetailResp.pTime else null`
(`OverviewFragment.kt:1055`). A bot with `state == "stopped"` and
`isHistory == false` therefore renders the 6-row history set with NO
stopped-time row; collapsing the two predicates adds a row legacy
never shows.

fields.name: sz
fields.doc:
Total committed order volume (wire `sz`,
`StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:136`).

This — NOT [`investment`](Self::investment) — is what the legacy
Overview "Accumulative amount" / "Invested amount" row renders on the
MARGIN slice (`TacticListDetailsDataMapper.kt:1637`, history `:1243`).
They are two distinct wire fields; do not substitute one for the other.

fields.name: invest_ccy
fields.doc:
Unit of the invested/accumulative amount (wire `investCcy`,
`StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:190`).

The invested-amount LABEL is suffixed from this field, not from
[`ccy`](Self::ccy): legacy passes it through
`BotConverter.getMarginUnit(investmentCcy = data.investCcy)`
(`TacticListDetailsDataMapper.kt:1644-1656`), while Total PnL and
Extra margin pass `ccy` through `getPnlUnit` (`:1447`, `:1699`).
`getMarginUnit` is a literal alias of `getPnlUnit`
(`BotConverter.kt:120-121`) and both return the passed ccy verbatim
when non-empty, so the wire field IS the entire difference between
those labels.

resolves the key directly.

fields.name: single_grid_amount_display
fields.doc:
"Amount per grid" (Parameters + Grid-orders) — strategy trade convertor
`toTargetFormatted(singleAmt).round` (HalfUp at the target-unit
precision); the unit join stays native.

**Do not consume this twin — call
`contract_grid_single_amount_display(inst_id, single_amt)` per render
instead.** Unlike every other twin here, this value depends on the
user's MUTABLE trade-unit preference (`resolve_stgy_amount_route` ->
`get_trade_unit`), not just on the instrument and the wire payload. A
value computed at parse time therefore goes stale as soon as the
preference changes and only heals on the next fetch/WS frame. Native
never snapshots it: `OKTConvertorProvider` empties its convertor cache
on `OKTNotificationTradeSettingWillChange`
(`OKTConvertorProvider.m:54, 66-72`) so each access rebuilds against
the current preference.

Kept (still computed) only because removing an exported Record field
deletes the Kotlin getter and fails Android `refer-check`. iOS moved off
it; Android should move to the funnel when it adopts this screen.

the three History count rows above already use.

fields.name: funding_fee_display
fields.doc:
History funding-fee row — fund-fee convertor chain `.down.suffix
.prependPlusSign` at `fundingFeeDig` (`.down` == NSRoundDown == floor).
Non-zero values are `Wrapped` with the BAKED `" <ccy>"` suffix and a
raw-sign "+" prefix (legacy `prependPlusSign` compares the ORIGINAL
decimal, so a tiny positive flooring to "0.00" still shows "+0.00");
exact zero → "0" WITH the baked `" <ccy>"` suffix — the ANDROID rule
(`getSpecialBotValue` appends the unit on every branch); iOS's zero
short-circuit drops it, recorded as entry 4 in the Divergence register;
legacy pnl color (truncate-toward-zero compare).
The ccy is baked here — there is deliberately NO separate unit field
(a `funding_fee_unit` sibling existed while the plan was a native-side
join; it was removed as zero-consumer surface once the suffix moved
into the twin).

fields.name: funding_fee_supported
fields.doc:
Whether funding fees apply to this instrument at all: SWAP always,
X-Perps too (a long-dated future that DOES charge funding), normal
delivery futures never.

A boolean, deliberately NOT baked into [`funding_fee_display`]. The
domain question ("do they apply") is Rust's; the glyph for `false` is
native's, and legacy's is an EMPTY string with the row still present
(`DealRecordPresenter.kt:228-236` adds it unconditionally,
`InformationItemBinder.kt:144` assigns the text with no dash mapping).
Baking the blank in would make the display field mean "the fee or a
sentinel" for every platform that reads it.

fields.name: history_grid_profit_display
fields.doc:
History grid-profit row — profit convertor chain `.useDynamicPrecision
.down.suffix.prependPlusSign` (linear profit precision 4 / inverse
`profitDig`). Non-zero → `Wrapped` with the BAKED `" <ccy>"` suffix and
raw-sign "+" prefix; zero/absent → "0" WITH the baked `" <ccy>"` suffix
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:143-147` concatenates the unit with no zero
test — Divergence register entry 4).

fields.name: earn_profit_display
fields.doc:
History Auto-Earn profit value — `formatAutoEarn(bot.common.autoEarn
.totalProfit, status, instId, instType, investUnit)` →
`getPnlAndColorPair(… isShowUnit = true, isQuoteCcy = true, digit = null,
minDigit = null)`. `Number` (never `Wrapped`): the unit rides alongside as
[`history_earn_unit`] because the sign is `ExceptZero` and the renderer's
`Wrapped` variant cannot carry that sign — the established units-slice
split. Empty profit → `Placeholder`.

fields.name: stake_profit_display
fields.doc:
History Auto-Staking profit value. Identical shape to
[`earn_profit_display`]; legacy routes it through `formatAutoStake`, which
differs from `formatAutoEarn` only in NOT threading `isHistory` — and
contract grid never threads it anyway (see [`show_earn_card`]).

fields.name: history_earn_unit
fields.doc:
Unit suffix shared by both rows — legacy's `investUnit`
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:299-305`):
`sourceCcy` when non-blank, else `getMarginCcy(instId, instType, feeCcy)`
= `feeCcy.ifNullOrEmptyOrBlank(instrument.getMarginSymbol())`
(`StrategyConvert.kt:184-192`).

fields.name: show_earn_card
fields.doc:
Whether the Auto-Earn row shows — legacy's `formatAutoEarn` null gate
`canShowEarnOrStakeProfit(totalProfit, status)`
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:494-502`).

NOTE the gate takes a third `isHistory` parameter that skips the
`status != "default"` leg, and this is the History tab — but contract grid
does NOT thread it: `ContractGridBenefitDataMapper` calls `formatAutoEarn`
with five POSITIONAL arguments (`:333-339`), so `isShowUnit`, `minDigit`
and `isHistory` all take their defaults and `isHistory` is `false`. Do not
"fix" this to the history-permissive form; it would show the row for a
`default`-status bot that legacy hides.

The `shouldShowAutoEarn` flavour gate (`!BotDiffHelper.isCrBotApp()`,
`StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:433-434`) stays in Kotlin, as it does for
contract DCA — it is an app-variant question, not a bot question.

This means "the earn VALUE exists", which for earn is the same as "some
earn row shows": `addAutoEarnProfit` (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1285`)
branches three ways under one outer `autoEarnProfit non-blank` check, and
every branch emits a row. WHICH row is a native decision and deliberately
not modelled here — the middle branch keys off `config.autoEarn` from
`BotConfigUseCase`, which Rust does not have, and the third emits an
`AUTO_SIMPLE_EARN` row with no VIP tag. Native reads
`bot.common.autoEarn.status` for that branch and for the VIP-tag
suppression on `vip_dropout`.

fields.name: show_stake_card
fields.doc:
Whether the Auto-Staking row shows.

STRICTER than [`show_earn_card`]'s rule, because the row is gated TWICE
and the second gate is not a restatement of the first. `formatAutoStake`
returns null unless `canShowEarnOrStakeProfit`, and then
`addAutoEarnOrStaking` (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1356`) additionally
requires:

```text
autoStakeProfit non-blank && autoStakeState != "default" && autoStakeState non-blank
```

The two differ for a real case: a bot with `totalProfit > 0` and status
`"default"` passes the value gate on the profit leg alone, so the value
exists — but the row gate then hides it. Using the value gate alone shows
a staking row legacy does not.

The `shouldShowAutoStake` flavour gate stays in Kotlin.

fields.name: last_price_display
fields.doc:

?.toLocalizedString()` (FuturesGridDetailsOverviewCellViewModel
.swift:298-309; HalfUp IS the OKTFormatter default): charge precision,
NO suffix — the ccy lives in the row label via [`quote_symbol`].
`Placeholder` when blank / cold store (legacy renders "--").

fields.name: liq_px_display
fields.doc:
Overview "Est liquidation price" — `OKTBotDigitalPrecisionUtil
.localString(forEstLiqPrice:price:direction:appendUnit: false)`
(FuturesGridDetailsOverviewCellViewModel.swift:381 →
OKTBotDigitalPrecisionUtil.m:262-278): direction "short" → Down,
anything else → Up, charge precision, NO unit — BOTH detail surfaces
pass `appendUnit: false` (the exported `contract_grid_liq_price_display`
funnel's suffixed shape is the place-order card, not this row).
`Placeholder` when blank / cold store (legacy nil-convertor / empty
formatted branches render "--").

fields.name: profit_list_failed

True when the `profit-list` fetch that fills [`profit_snapshots`] FAILED,
as opposed to the server genuinely returning no history. Both leave the
series empty, so without this the chart hides identically for a brand-new
bot and a network error and native cannot offer a retry.

`#[serde(skip)]` because it is not a wire field: set post-fetch by
`fetch_contract_bot_info` and carried across WS frames by

`SpotGridOverviewData::profit_items_failed`, which lives on its

(`isUsingUSDTProfitDisplay == false`): values from the top-level

hardcoded `marginPerCcyInfo["USDT"]` bucket, both convertors replaced by

absent bucket yields all-`Placeholder`); iOS reads it ONLY behind its

fields.name: overview_available_ccys
fields.doc:
The unit options the Overview may offer, in the order native shows them:
`[margin_ccy, "USDT"]` when the four-leg coin-margined gate passes, and
EMPTY otherwise. Legacy hardcodes exactly these two
(`CoinMarginedCcyDisplay.COIN(0)` / `USDT(1)`).

Rust decides only WHETHER the toggle is offered and WHICH units it
offers. Which one is selected stays native's, per the ownership rule
documented on [`ContractGridOverviewMoneyDisplay`]: the selection is
persisted per `algoId` and shared with the bot LIST page, and mirroring
it into Rust would give one persisted value two owners.

sits in different positions in different arms. Native renders this
sequence as given.

fields.doc:
The Overview field grid rendered in the MARGIN currency — the default
slice, and the only one a linear bot has.

Two baked slices rather than one mutable selection, matching the
ownership rule already documented on
[`ContractGridOverviewMoneyDisplay`]: the persisted unit choice lives in
native's per-`algoId` store, shared with the bot LIST page, so mirroring
it into Rust would give one persisted value two owners. Native picks a
slice with the same single branch it already uses for the money
displays.

fields.name: overview_rows_usdt
fields.doc:
The same grid rendered in USDT. Populated only when the four-leg
coin-margined gate passes — EMPTY otherwise, which is native's signal
that there is no alternate slice to offer.

Row membership and ORDER are identical to
[`overview_rows`](Self::overview_rows); only the values and the three
unit-suffixed labels differ.

fields.name: overview_invested_amount_display
fields.doc:
The Overview "Accumulative amount" value for the MARGIN slice, formatted
from wire [`sz`](Self::sz).

Deliberately NOT
[`ContractGridOverviewMoneyDisplay::investment`], which is formatted from
wire `investment`. Those are two different quantities and legacy Android
renders `sz` on this row (`TacticListDetailsDataMapper.kt:1635`, history
`:1242`) — as this struct's own `sz` doc already states. The shared
money-slice field is left untouched because it is the iOS consumer's
source and that platform's oracle is a different file; correcting the row
here rather than there fixes Android without moving an iOS number.

fields.name: overview_grid_profit_display
fields.doc:
The Overview "Grid profit" value for the MARGIN slice, honouring the
source-currency preference.

Legacy prefers `gridProfitInSourceCcy` over `gridProfit` whenever
`sourceCcy` is non-blank, on the margin slice only
(`TacticListDetailsDataMapper.kt:1475-1494`). The shared money slice reads
`gridProfit` unconditionally, which shows the wrong currency's MAGNITUDE —
not a rounding difference — on any bot with a source currency. Corrected
here rather than in that slice, which is the iOS consumer's source and is
oracled to a different platform.

fields.name: overview_grid_profit_raw
fields.doc:

Legacy's exact-zero substitution tests the PREFERRED raw, so the two must

fields.name: overview_unpaired_pnl_display

has not resolved yet. Native silently returns (log only, no toast) — the
iOS layer suppresses the toast for THIS variant; it exists so `can_submit`
stays false until the auto-reserve-utilisation result arrives.

variants.name: Invalid

direction, leverage) that has no dedicated variant. `message` is the

invalid-input string. These cases are gated by the input UI upstream
and are not normally user-reachable at submit time.

doc:
Structured L2 validation failure for the Contract Grid place-order flow.

Issue #16: Rust must NOT ship user-facing localized strings — native owns
localization. This enum is carried as data in `validation_error` (it is a
`uniffi::Enum`, not a thrown `uniffi::Error`, so it needs NO
`From<UnexpectedUniFFICallbackError>` impl). Native maps each variant to an
EXISTING localized string; params (`max_available` / `min_investment`) are
carried raw so native can format the templated message.

name: DcaTimelineStreamUseCase
doc:
Lean, cross-variant timeline-streaming surface for native.

Wraps **only** the WS-backed trade-list timeline engine (HTTP trade-list
seed + `algo-spot-dca` / `algo-contract-dca` WS + avgPx-change refetch)
already composed by [`OKTSDcaCommonService`]. Unlike
`SpotDcaTimelineInteractor` / `ContractDcaTimelineInteractor`, it does NOT
re-fetch bot info or position (the detail interactor owns those) and carries
no end-cycle / cancel actions. A single object serves both Spot and Contract
DCA via `is_spot_dca`.

This is a deliberate `uniffi::Object` promotion (the broader
`OKTSDcaCommonService` facade stays demoted): it restores the native-callable
surface that iOS `RustDCATradeListStreamUseCase` consumed before its 2026-02
app-size removal. The streaming engine itself was never deleted.

documented as. `getAmountSymbolWithFallback` (StrategyConvert.kt:843-855)
hands `ctVal` to `getBotAmountUnit`, which uses it only on the FUTURES
`setCtVal` leg (:830-832) — that moves the converted NUMBER, not the symbol
— and its blank-symbol fallback is
`InstrumentCurrencyUtils.getBaseCurrency(instId, instType)` (:851), an instId
derivation like `price_unit_from_inst_id`. The History expanded card emits
both amount cells as funnel cells (`unit: None`), so native resolves the
unit per render via `contract_grid_amount_unit(inst_id)`, which still
answers `None` on a cold store / delisted instrument — that amount-side
fallback is NOT ported today.

leg is already ported as `price_unit_from_inst_id`

(see `StopType::StopAndKeepStaking`'s doc comment).

name: reset_form
doc:
Return the form to the state a freshly-opened page starts from.

The page's own reset (`resetRecurringItem`, which replaces the ObjC item
wholesale after a successful order or a pair change) had no counterpart
here, so this state OUTLIVED the page: a fresh page carried the previous
order's basket and its ratios. That is not cosmetic — `set_coins` keeps a
survivor's EXISTING ratio, so a single-coin re-entry could inherit 50%
from the order just placed and post `ratio: "0.50"` for a lone asset.

Network results are cleared too: whatever refetches after a reset is what
should populate them, and a stale balance beside a fresh form is exactly
the pairing this avoids.

name: set_coin_ratios
doc:
Write every coin's ratio in ONE state publish.

Exists for editors that collect a whole allocation before committing it — a
sheet that cannot stream state back per keystroke, so it hands over the
finished split. Looping one-coin batches is not equivalent: each call
publishes, so the basket would be seen at intermediate totals, and a later
call being refused would leave the earlier ones applied.

**All-or-nothing.** The batch is rejected outright if any ratio is out of
`0..=100`, any coin is not in the basket, or any coin appears twice. Applying
the acceptable subset would leave a total that is not 100, which the user
cannot correct without re-editing — refusing keeps the last good allocation.

`reload_min_amount`; `Loading` after the action's sync flip;
`Success` on Ok; `Error` on Err. Native reads this for the
loading / error / success transitions.

while idle / loading / on success. Native owns the surrounding
localized copy; Rust holds only the raw error text.

fields.name: submit_state
fields.doc:
FSM for the multi-order submit. `Idle` before any submit; `Loading`
after the action's sync flip; `Success` / `Error` on completion.
Enum-typed, so it carries **no** `#[uniffi(default)]` — a bare
`#[uniffi(default)]` on an enum field compiles under cargo and then
breaks bindgen for both Swift and Kotlin.

fields.name: submit_error
fields.doc:
Raw underlying error text from the submit — `None` while idle /
loading / on success. Native owns the surrounding localized copy and
dispatches on the error code it already received via the vended
place-order error handler; Rust holds only the raw text.

fields.name: submit_error_code
fields.doc:
Positive business code (`sCode`) of a rejected submit, as a string —
`None` on success, while idle/loading, and for transport-level failures.
Same shape as `interactors/dca/contract_dca/edit_params.rs:216`.

Native's vended place-order error handler DISPATCHES ON THIS
(`OKTPOErrorHandler.m:56-111`): five branches key off `error.code`, and the
generic arm resolves its copy through `[OKTPODataFactory poErrorInfo:error.code]`
before falling back to the message. Reporting the failure as `submit_error`
alone dropped the one field that decides what the user sees, which is half of
why a rejection could produce no affordance at all (QA #14).

fields.name: submit_algo_id
fields.doc: `algoId` of the accepted order. Empty until a submit succeeds.

fields.name: left_lever
fields.doc:
Leg leverage, as the raw string the form shows.

Added for Wave C1's final batch: when `OKTSArbLegContentHost` takes over
`OKTPOContextDataDelegate`, it must source every context value from Rust
instead of reading it back off native's child VCs. Every other member
already had a state field; `lever` was the one gap
(`OKTASPOContentVC.m:912` reads `buttonLineVC.leverValue` into
`params.lever` on the pre-check sheet).

Not on the submit wire — the multi-order body carries no `lever`
(`getCommitArbitrageParams` never sets it). Pre-check display only, so an
empty value must stay empty rather than defaulting to `"1"`, which would
assert a leverage the user never chose.

fields.name: left_direction
fields.doc:
Raw `OKTASPODirectionValue` the leg's direction control currently shows.

This is the SINGLE source for the leg's direction: [`Self::left_side`] and
[`Self::left_pos_side`] are derived from it by
[`ArbitragePlaceOrderActions::set_left_direction`], so side and posSide can
never disagree with the identity the user picked. Before Wave C1 the native
direction VC owned the identity and pushed side/posSide separately, which
is exactly the shape that let them drift.

Empty until the direction control seeds it. Empty is NOT coerced to a
default direction — an unset direction must read as unset, or the confirm
sheet would show a direction the user never chose.

fields.name: right_direction

computed or when the price-type branch returned nothing.

fields.name: right_computed_price
fields.doc:
Computed leg price as a decimal string. Empty when not yet
computed or when the price-type branch returned nothing.

fields.name: spread_rate_value

Spread rate `(left - right) / right` as a decimal string. Empty
when `spread_rate_valid` is false.

fields.name: spread_rate_display
fields.doc:
Display twin of [`Self::spread_rate_value`].

The raw field is the unscaled ratio `(left - right) / right`; native shows
a SIGNED PERCENT. Before this twin existed the iOS Rust arm passed the raw
ratio straight into the shared price-settings label, so a spread native
rendered as `+0.31%` appeared as `0.0030749…`.

Native leaf (`OKTArbStgyUtil.getDepthSpreadRateText`, m:31-42):
`[[gap okt_divide:right].treatAsPercentage.prependPlusSign
toLocalizedStringDownToMax:2]`, with `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder` ("--")
when either input string is empty.

Three-way, matching native's three outcomes exactly:
- `None` — the two legs' quote currencies differ. Native calls
`updateSpreadRateWith:@""` (no text at all), NOT the "--" placeholder.
- `Some(Placeholder)` — units match but an input is absent/unparseable →
native's `kOKTPOEmptyPlaceholder`.
- `Some(Percent{..})` — the real value.

Enum-typed → **no `#[uniffi(default)]`** (a bare one compiles under cargo
then breaks bindgen on both platforms).

fields.name: left_avail
fields.doc:
Base-converted ENTER price as a decimal string. Empty when
unparseable; never coerced to zero (see `money_math.md`).
One leg's `/max-available` rows, or `None` before the first response.

`None` is load-bearing: it is the pre-first-fetch state, in which native has
no commit handler and every KV row renders its own `--` placeholder. A
default-filled row would instead render five zeros, which reads as real data.

fields.name: left_margin_infos
fields.doc:
One leg's `/leverage-info` rows — native's `marginInfoArr`.

An EMPTY vec is the legitimate "no leverage rows" state (not-logged-in, or a
biz with no leverage), which is why this is a plain `Vec` and not an
`Option`: `marginInfoByPosSide:` returns nil for both "never fetched" and
"fetched, no rows", so native cannot tell them apart either and the lever
control renders the same placeholder for both.

fields.name: right_enter_px_base
fields.doc: Base-converted ENTER price as a decimal string.

doc:

Unit-suffixed labels use the synthetic `<key>_ccy` `FormattedCDKey` +
`ccy` param convention.

The `ccy` param is resolved PER ROW, never from one shared unit: legacy
draws on three different wire fields — `investCcy` for InvestedAmount
(:1645), `ccy` for TotalPnl (:1451) and ExtraMargin (:1699), and the
quote ccy for LastPrice (:1719). `getMarginUnit` and `getPnlUnit` are
literal aliases of one another (`BotConverter.kt:120-121`) that return
the passed ccy verbatim, so the wire field IS the whole difference.

fields.doc:

`nextLineText`, :1348/:1510).

ArbitrageAndTotalApr must leave this EMPTY even though it renders two
legs: its split-colour binder path never calls
`nextLineTextView.setTextOrGone` (`BotListFieldDataBinder.kt:235-254`),
so a recycled row would keep stale next-line text. The next line also
cannot carry its own colour — the binder assigns one `tvColor` to both
views (:257-271).

fields.doc:
Which drawable the icon channel shows.

LastPrice with a blank price sets this to `None` while leaving
[`enabled`](Self::enabled) `true`: legacy clears only `ivDrawableType`
(:1723) and never disables the row, so expressing that through `enabled`
would re-conflate the two affordances this pair exists to separate.

fields.name: label_intent
fields.doc:
LABEL-tap action, when the label opens a sheet rather than a tooltip.

Native must derive `subItemType` from `tooltip.is_some() ||
label_intent.is_some()`, because `BotListFieldDataBinder` gates the label
click on `subItemType` (:176-180) — keying off `tooltip` alone, as spot
does, would leave GridProfit's label tap dead.

doc:
One Contract Grid Overview field-grid row.

Shape follows [`SpotGridOverviewRowPresentation`] with TWO additions,
because contract rows carry two INDEPENDENT affordances that spot's single
channel cannot express: GridProfit has a label sheet AND a withdraw icon
(:1513 + :1514), and ExtraMargin has a label tooltip AND an edit icon
(:1698 + :1699).

[`intent`](Self::intent) deliberately keeps SPOT'S meaning — the ICON
channel — because spot's shipped binder wires `row.intent` to
`ivDrawableType` and `contentDrawableClick` while routing `row.tooltip` to
`subItemClick`. The new channel is therefore named
[`label_intent`](Self::label_intent) rather than redefining `intent`, so the
identically-named field cannot mean opposite things on the two records.

differently (raw ccy as the label, a skipped block, a blank balance row, a
precision of 2) and collapsing those into one in-band default here would have
changed four behaviours at once.

Numeric-looking fields stay STRINGS, deliberately. `coin_id` and `size_dig`
are wire strings on `TradeCoinInfo`, and both native call sites parse them
with their own fallback (`Int(coinId)` guarding an early return, `Int(sizeDig)

needs the number-tolerant reader; a plain `String` field fails the payload outright.

read by the current (buggy) Android consumer:
`SmartArbitrageProfitsFragment.kt:481`'s "Open spread" row,
`info?.openSpreadProfit`. The REAL data for that row is
`bot.smart_arbitrage.open_cost.spread_amt` (see [`SmartArbCostInfo`] and
[`SmartArbBotSpecificInfo::open_cost`]) — a different, nested wire path.
Cannot be deleted unilaterally: removing a `pub` field from a shipped
`uniffi::Record` is FFI-breaking, and the field is still referenced above.
Repoint the Android row to a straight `open_cost.spread_amt` read (no
summing — see [`SmartArbCostInfo::spread_amt`]'s doc comment) and remove
this field in a separate, coordinated change once that lands.

fields.doc: Server-localized display string.

doc:
One selectable scheduled-check period offered by `GET /priapi/v5/algo/public/config`'s `intervalOptions`
list (ALGO-43412 combined mode). Only bot types supporting combined rebalance return the field.

`key` is the period in MINUTES and is what gets submitted as the bot's `interval`; both natives map it straight
into their own option models (Android `IntervalOption(key: Int)`, iOS `options.map { $0.key }`), which is why it is
`i32` and not `u32` — `u32` would generate `kotlin.UInt` and force casts on the Android side, and `i64` would
generate `kotlin.Long`. `value` is the label ALREADY localised by the server and is rendered verbatim: natives
have no client-side formatter, so rows with a blank `value` are filtered out during projection and every option
reaching native is displayable. The list is honestly empty when the server omits the field — no fallback is
seeded here.

`Eq` is the one addition to the neighbouring records' derive set: `SmartPortfolioPublicConfig` holds a
`Vec<IntervalOptionInfo>` and already derives `Eq`, which a `PartialEq`-only element type would break.

**Gap R-F5 (Wave R3).** Modelled solely so the Rust arm can satisfy
`OKTSpotOrderCcyProviding.okts_spot_feeCcy()`, whose native conformance is
`feeList.first?.feeCcy` (`OKTInstrumentDisplayUtil.swift:923`). The Invest-More
and Edit-Amount sheet factories take a `model:` argument typed as that
protocol composition, so without this field the Rust arm has no way to supply
a conforming object built from typed data — forcing the legacy
`OKTStgyInfoModel` to be threaded through purely for one string.

Deliberately narrow: only `feeCcy` is modelled. The wire entry carries more,
but nothing on the detail path reads it, and `public_types.md`'s
promote-on-demand rule says model what a consumer needs, not what the payload
holds.

are meant to total 100% (e.g. a server even-split 0.3333×3 → 33/33/34). A genuine
user deficit/surplus is left as-is so native's "remaining" stays truthful. Shared
across iOS + Android so the rounding policy can't drift per platform.

fields.name: allocation_status
fields.doc:
Coin-allocation validity classified from `allocation_display_percents`
(Valid / Deficit / Surplus / Empty). Lets native drive the red border +
prompt off one Rust status instead of re-deriving the `== 100%` rule.

array by `triggerAction == "start"` — the Rust port of native
`OKTStgyInfoModel.startTriggerModel` (`OKTStgyInfoModel.m:131-136`).

entirely). Native's getter returns nil there, every `isIndicator*`
message to nil answers `NO`, and the Info tab's Start Condition row
falls through to `--` with no tap affordance — identical rendering to
`Some(_)` with `indicator == Unsupported`. Both states are preserved
rather than flattened so a "server sent nothing" bug stays
distinguishable from "server sent a literal we don't render".

Appended field — `#[uniffi(default = None)]` keeps the pre-existing
Swift construction site (`SmartIcebergDetailNativeProvider.swift:319`)
source-compatible across the bindings regen, per ffi-evolution rule 3.
The literal is spelled out because a bare `#[uniffi(default)]` breaks
bindgen on both platforms.

⚠️ Deliberately DIFFERENT from [`Self::average_price_round_display`],
which formats the **same** `avg_px` with HALF_UP for the multi-coin
aggregate line. Native genuinely uses two rounding directions for one
wire value (cell: `toLocalizedStringDown`; aggregate:
`chargeConvertor.toQuoteFormated(avgPx).round`). Asserted as a divergence
in the tests — do not "unify" them.

Swift row (the unit lives on the parent as `quote_unit`).

separate `OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.pnlColor(withPnl:precision:)` call — one
derivation instead of two, so text and colour cannot disagree.

A7 — this coin's ratio **as the Overview AGGREGATE line renders it**:
`treatAsPercentage` → `toLocalizedStringRoundToMax:2` (HALF-UP, max 2,
trailing zeros dropped).

**Finding R-B20.** Deliberately a SECOND twin over the same `ratio`
field: the allocation **cell** renders it *uncapped*
(`.treatAsPercentage().toLocalizedString()`,
`RecurringBuyCryptoAllocationCellInfoViewState.swift:147-148`) while the
aggregate line rounds to 2 (`OKTSOrderListUtil.m`,
`OKTSRecurringDisplayTypeRatio`). Collapsing them into one value rendered
`"33.333%"` on the aggregate line where native shows `"33.33%"`.

Same deliberate-divergence shape as
[`Self::average_price_display`] (FLOOR, cell) vs
[`Self::average_price_round_display`] (HALF_UP, aggregate) — do not merge
either pair.

fields.name: cell_ratio_display

`treatAsPercentage().toLocalizedString()`.

The cell half of the R-B20 pair. [`Self::aggregate_ratio_display`] is the
aggregate half and rounds HALF-UP at 2. Do not merge them.

variants.name: Transitioning
variants.doc:
Every wire value other than `running` and `stopped` — recognized transitional
states (`stopping`, `starting`, `opening`, `closing`, `risking`, `canceled`,
`effective`, ...) and any unrecognized string alike. Legacy shows
`[WithdrawProfit, Rename, Stop]` for all of them (no `ReducePositions`, which is
gated on `state == running` specifically), so that is what this bucket derives.

doc:
Action-relevant lifecycle after the raw `state` wire string has been classified by
`smart_arbitrage_action_lifecycle_from_wire`.

**This enum is total by design, not an allowlist of recognized states.** Legacy has
no state allowlist for the Smart Arbitrage detail-page menu — it has exactly two
conditions: `TacticListDetailsDataMapper` diverts on `isHistory || state ==
STATE_STOPPED`; everything else (`running`, `stopping`, `starting`, the
Smart-Arbitrage-specific `opening` / `closing` / `risking` sub-states
(`TacticsUiConst.SmartArbState`), `canceled`, `effective`, and any string the backend
adds later that this classifier has never seen) takes the *same* pending-data branch
with the real button list (`PROFIT_WITHDRAWAL`, `SMART_ARB_REDUCE_POSITION` only when
`state == STATE_RUNNING`, `STOP`) plus the tail Rename splice.

So only `Running` and `Stopped` are distinguished; `Transitioning` is the catch-all
for every other wire value, recognized or not. `Unknown` is deliberately NOT a fourth,
fail-closed bucket here — see `derive_smart_arbitrage_action_catalog`'s doc comment
for why an earlier revision of this classifier had one and why it was removed.

`unit` distinguishes two cases native does NOT treat alike:

interpolation, NOT the RTL-aware `OKTStringF.appendSymbol`. Reproducing
the raw join is parity; switching to the RTL-aware one would be an
undeclared behaviour change in RTL locales.

fields.name: stop_attempt
fields.doc:
Monotonic id of the most recent `stop_bot()` invocation — SB-X02.

## Why a counter is needed at all

`stop_state` / `stop_error` are STICKY: they settle at
`Success`/`Error` and stay there until the next invocation. A foreign
consumer therefore cannot distinguish "the terminal I am already showing"
from "a new terminal that happens to look identical", because a
UniFFI Record state cannot be mutated from the foreign side — there is
nothing for the consumer to clear.

Consumers work around that by latching on the value, which silently
swallows two consecutive IDENTICAL failures — exactly the case a user hits
by retrying a failing action. Pairing the terminal with this id makes each
invocation distinguishable: latch on `(attempt, state)`, not on `state`.

## Bumped on EVERY invocation, including the rejected ones

The pre-validation branch in each action is itself a terminal and reaches
`Error` with no `Loading` in between, so a repeated rejection would
otherwise produce no state change whatsoever. The bump lives inside the
same `modify_state` as each branch's own writes, so it costs no extra
observer notification.

Wraps rather than saturates: identity only needs to CHANGE, and a
saturated counter would stop changing.

Additive — `#[uniffi(default = 0)]` keeps every existing foreign
construction site compiling.

`timeframe`, `trigger_cond`) only populate when indicator is RSI.
* `trigger_px` and `delay_seconds` only populate for price triggers
(delay also for RSI).

name: recurring_charge_currency_price_digit
doc:
The charge-currency `price_dig` for one instrument family.

Replaces the last use of `OKTBiz.createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` in the Recurring
buy-price sheet, which read `.quotePrecision` off the returned convertor to cap the text
field's decimals.

The equivalence is exact for spot, checked in the source rather than assumed:
`OKTSpotCommon.createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` (`OKTBiz.m:1575-1580`) builds
`OKTSimpleChargeConvertor` with `precision: cc.priceDig.integerValue`, where `cc` is
`getChargeCurrencyForInstFamily:` — the same charge currency and the same `price_dig`
that [`resolve_price_digit`] reads. So `quotePrecision == price_dig` on this path, and
the two price funnels above already round at that digit.

`0` for an unresolved family, which is native's own number there rather than a chosen
default. `createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` never returns nil — it allocs
unconditionally, so a missing charge currency reaches `cc.priceDig.integerValue`
through ObjC nil-messaging and yields `precision: 0`.

Do NOT continue that sentence into "so the Swift `?? 2` beside the read only ever
covered a missing spot-biz OBJECT, a branch with no analogue once `OKTrade` is gone".
That inference is what dropped the cushion and shipped the P0: it compares the two
VALUES and ignores the two STORES. Native's biz is warmed before the running-bots list
renders (`OKTStrategyLiveOrdersDataSource.m:541` calls `loadBiz:` per order inst type),
so its `0` was near-unreachable. core-trading's spot biz is warmed on the Rust detail
screen (`info_stream_use_case.rs` awaits the preload) but by nothing on the
running-bots-list route, which is where `0` became the usual answer.

Value parity is not behaviour parity when the two sources are warmed differently.

`0` also keeps the absence semantics of the two funnels above, so those two cannot
disagree with each other. That is NOT a whole-screen invariant: a caller that takes the
input-cap variant below deliberately breaks it — iOS's buy-price sheet caps at 2 while
its market-price label still renders at 0.

## Do not use this one to cap a text field

The `0` is a display convention, and applying it to an input cap is what
produced a P0: the buy-price sheet locked its fields to zero decimals AND
prefilled the saved bounds rounded to integers, so a stored 0.42-0.87 range
opened as 0-1 and Confirm submitted that (iOS `9e78f4423`, reachable from the
running-bots list, which primes nothing). `0` is also a legitimate digit for
an integer-priced instrument, so the caller cannot tell the two apart here.
Use [`recurring_charge_currency_price_digit_warmed`], which waits for the
store and answers `None` when the family genuinely did not resolve.

name: convert_contract_dca_size_to_display_unit
doc:
Convert a contract-denominated size to the user's display unit, for native surfaces
that render a size Rust does not already ship converted.

`ContractDcaPositionLiveState.display_size` covers the position HEADER, whose size is
part of that interactor's state. Other surfaces render sizes that are not on any Rust
state -- the ongoing-tab parameter rows, the close-position sheet -- and those called
OKTradeCore's `tradeConvertor.toTargetFormatted(..)` / `getBotAmount(..)` to do it.
That call is a UNIT CONVERSION, i.e. arithmetic, i.e. Rust's under the convertor RFC
section 3.4, so this exposes the conversion rather than the multiplier.

Returns `None` (never zero) when the instrument or the conversion is unavailable, so
the caller shows its placeholder instead of a fabricated number. Pair the result with
the `amount` convertor role for rounding and the unit label.

One FFI crossing per value. Fine for a handful of rows; memoize on the native side if
a surface ever renders these per list item on a scroll path.

digit `0`, mirroring native's `Int(precision) ?? 0` on a cold store.

name: RecurringCoinRatio
doc:
One coin in the plan being edited.

# Why the ratio is whole percent here and a fraction on the wire

The native editing model (`OKTRecurringItem.recurringRate`) is an
integer 0-100, and its even-split rule depends on integer division and
remainder (`100/n` with the remainder spread over the tail, e.g. six
coins become 16/16/17/17/17/17). Holding the same integer keeps that
arithmetic exact and keeps Rust's rounding identical to the shipped
behaviour. The order endpoint wants a decimal fraction, so
[`to_order_coin_params`] converts on the way out — by integer
formatting, never through a float.
One coin's allocation, for the batch write [`RecurringBuyPlaceOrderActions::set_coin_ratios`].

Deliberately carries ONLY the ratio. `RecurringSelectedCoin` would compile here
but also carries `min_price`/`max_price`, and a caller that does not know about
price bounds would blank them on every write. Recurring's bounds currently live
only in the ObjC mirror, so that would be latent rather than live — but a record
that cannot express the mistake is better than one that relies on the field
staying unused.

`ratio_percent` is whole percent, matching `RecurringSelectedCoin`. No decimal
fraction crosses here — that conversion belongs to `apply_recommendation`, which
receives a *server* plan.

name: execute_stop_with_options
doc:
Execute the stop with full, explicit control over which optional
wire fields are present. Additive sibling to [`Self::execute_stop`] /
[`Self::execute_stop_with_condition`] — those two always emit
`instId` and `algoOrdType` (when the interactor holds them) and
require a concrete `StopType`, which cannot represent legacy Smart
Arbitrage's two stop paths:

- `BotOperatorButtonDisposer`'s minimal "close bots" dispatch sends
`StrategyStopReq(algoId)` alone — no `instId`, no `algoOrdType`,
no `stopType`.
- `SmartArbiStopConfirmDialog` sends `algoOrdType` but never
`instId`, and omits `stopType` for the sell-all case (only the
keep-staking case sends a concrete `stopType`).

Parameters:
- `stop_type = None` omits the `stopType` key entirely — distinct
from `Some(StopType::StopAndSell)`, which callers must not use as
an "omit" stand-in (that conflation is exactly the wire-parity
risk this method exists to remove, even though
`SmartArbStopRequestBody` happens to also omit the key for
`StopAndSell` today — see that type's doc comment). `Some(t)`
sends `t`'s wire value.
- `include_inst_id = false` omits `instId` even though the
interactor was constructed with a real `inst_id` — both Smart
Arbitrage stop paths never populate `instId` on the legacy
request.
- `include_ord_type = false` omits `algoOrdType` — only the minimal
"close bots" path needs this; the confirm-dialog path keeps it.

Grid/DCA and any existing caller of the plain two methods are
unaffected — this method's behavior is opt-in per call site.

fields.name: convertors
fields.doc:
Role-keyed display convertors for this instrument + the user's size-unit
setting, applied by native to the raw values it already holds.

`None` means NOT YET RESOLVED — native must keep its legacy formatting
until a set arrives. This is deliberately an `Option` rather than a
defaulted value: `ContractDcaConvertors::default()` carries `precision: 0`,
which both renderers apply as max-fraction-digits, so publishing it would
TRUNCATE every price and size to an integer (`62183.45` -> `62,183`,
`0.0035` -> `0`) rather than pass values through. Precision 0 is also a
legitimate resolved value for a contract size, so native cannot tell the
two apart from the number alone — the absence has to be modelled.

Resolution is retried until it succeeds: the `instId` may arrive with
bot_info rather than the nav param (Android seeds it empty), and on a
cold-process deeplink the shared instrument store is not warm yet. See
`resolve_convertors_for`.

This is the replacement for native deciding precision/rounding/unit off
its own OKTradeCore convertors — see
`docs/rfcs/detail-convertor-surface.md`. It does NOT replace `raw_json`:
the blob stays as the VALUE path (§1.2), this fixes only the FORMAT path.

branch instead of merely being unrecognised.

`else` — a constant, with the cancel *value* never read — and `getCurState`
falls through to `getGridTacticsState(state)`
(`TacticListDataMapper.kt:5406`, `:5490`; `StrategyConvert.kt:1494-1520`).

marker view and share-chart util on the same shared code path).

```ignore
let handle = OKTSSmartArbitrageService::new().bot_stop_service();
let interactor = StopBotInteractor::create(algo_id, inst_id, StopBotType::SmartArbitrage, handle);
```

has no precompute-stop endpoint (`action_service.rs`'s

defensively if it's ever called anyway, mirroring the existing
force-sell skip-`start()` convention). Call `execute_stop` /
`execute_stop_with_condition` directly instead.
